Critical

Microsoft's durabletask PyPI Package Compromised in Supply Chain Attack

StepSecurity
2026-06-05 15 use cases 2 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Three malicious versions of Microsoft's official durabletask Python SDK were published to PyPI on May 19, 2026. The compromised package silently downloads and executes a 28 KB payload that steals credentials from AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, password managers, and over 90 developer tool configurations, then spreads laterally through cloud infrastructure. The payload skips systems with a Russian locale, a hallmark of Eastern European cybercrime operations. The attack has been linked to the TeamPCP threat group behind the Mini Shai-Hulud campaign.

[LLM] Pip install of compromised Microsoft durabletask versions 1.4.1-1.4.3 Delivery High
Hunts for pip / python invocations that explicitly request or have resolved to the three trojanized durabletask versions published to PyPI on 19 May 2026. Targets Linux CI runners, build agents, and cloud workloads where the package would be picked up. Rationale: Anchored on the three article-confirmed malicious versions (1.4.1, 1.4.2, 1.4.3) and the publication window of 19 May 2026 16:19 UTC onward. Process telemetry of explicit `pip install durabletask==X.Y.Z` invocations is high-fidelity since the legitimate prior version is 1.4.0 (Apr 8). Tier=alerting because of specific version pins. No external sources cross-checked.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1078
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "durabletask"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "install"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pip","pip3","python","python3") or FileName in~ ("pip","pip3","python","python3")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("durabletask==1.4.1","durabletask==1.4.2","durabletask==1.4.3")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "durabletask" and ProcessCommandLine !has "durabletask==1.4.0" and ProcessCommandLine !has "durabletask<1.4.1" and Timestamp between (datetime(2026-05-19) .. datetime(2026-05-20T12:00:00Z)))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3","python","python3")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "durabletask" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "install"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("durabletask==1.4.1","durabletask==1.4.2","durabletask==1.4.3")
   or (ActingProcessCommandLine !has "durabletask==1.4.0" and TimeGenerated between (datetime(2026-05-19) .. datetime(2026-05-20T12:00:00Z)))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] rope.pyz dropper executed as /tmp/managed.pyz from durabletask import Installation High
Hunts the unique payload-execution fingerprint from the TeamPCP supply chain attack: a python3 process whose command line references /tmp/managed.pyz, typically spawned via start_new_session=True from a parent python3 -c "import durabletask". Highest-fidelity single signal in the campaign. Rationale: /tmp/managed.pyz is the article-confirmed payload filename the dropper writes via urllib.request.urlretrieve and immediately executes with subprocess.Popen(["python3", "/tmp/managed.pyz"]). The string is unique to this campaign — virtually zero benign use of that exact path. Parent-process pivot on `python3 -c "import durabletask"` adds the chain-of-custody. No external sources cross-checked.
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1204.003 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
   or (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "import durabletask" and FileName in~ ("python","python3"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp asc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
   or (ParentProcessCommandLine has "import durabletask" and ActingProcessName in~ ("python","python3"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated asc

[LLM] Egress to TeamPCP rope.pyz C2 infrastructure (check.git-service.com / t.m-kosche.com / 160.119.64.3) Command & Control High
Detects DNS lookups or outbound network connections to the article-confirmed C2 domains used to fetch the rope.pyz dropper and to identify the Mini Shai-Hulud campaign. Single-hit alerting; these IOCs have no legitimate use. Rationale: Three article-confirmed IOCs with no legitimate use: check.git-service.com (hosts rope.pyz), t.m-kosche.com (secondary attribution beacon tying to TeamPCP Mini Shai-Hulud), and resolving IP 160.119.64.3 (HostUS / AS7489, AFRINIC). Domain `git-service.com` was registered via NameSilo 16 May 2026 — only 3 days before the attack — so trailing-day FPs are vanishingly unlikely. No external sources cross-checked.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic Web
let bad_domains = dynamic(["check.git-service.com","git-service.com","t.m-kosche.com","m-kosche.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (bad_domains) or RemoteIP == "160.119.64.3"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let bad_domains = dynamic(["check.git-service.com","git-service.com","t.m-kosche.com","m-kosche.com"]);
let dns = ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any (bad_domains)
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName, Source="DNS";
let net = ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
  | where DstHostname has_any (bad_domains) or DstIpAddr == "160.119.64.3"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery=DstHostname, DnsResponseName=DstIpAddr, Source="NET";
union isfuzzy=true dns, net
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] gh auth token / gpg-decrypt credential harvesting by python3 child Actions on Objectives High
Detects the rope.pyz collector pattern of harvesting GitHub Personal Access Tokens via gh CLI and GPG-protected secrets via `gpg --batch --passphrase anon --decrypt`, parented by a python3 process — exactly the cmdline strings the article ties to managed.pyz parallel collectors. Rationale: Article-verbatim cmdline strings: `gh auth token`, `gh auth status --show-token`, and `gpg --batch --passphrase anon --decrypt`. The literal passphrase `anon` is an attacker-chosen string with no legitimate use — humans do not use that passphrase for real GPG-protected material. Parented by python3 narrows out interactive developer use of gh. No external sources cross-checked.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.005 T1555 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3")
| where (FileName =~ "gh" and (ProcessCommandLine has "auth token" or ProcessCommandLine has "auth status --show-token"))
   or (FileName =~ "gpg" and ProcessCommandLine has_all ("--batch","--passphrase anon","--decrypt"))
| summarize CommandCount = count(),
            Commands = make_set(ProcessCommandLine),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
         by DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| where CommandCount >= 1
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName in~ ("python","python3")
| where (ActingProcessName =~ "gh" and (ActingProcessCommandLine has "auth token" or ActingProcessCommandLine has "auth status --show-token"))
   or (ActingProcessName =~ "gpg" and ActingProcessCommandLine has_all ("--batch","--passphrase anon","--decrypt"))
| summarize CommandCount = count(),
            Commands = make_set(ActingProcessCommandLine),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
         by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessId, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by FirstSeen desc
title: rope.pyz Credential Harvest - gh auth token / gpg anon decrypt from python3
id: 91c47e2b-3d18-46f7-a8e4-5b2c91d8af4e
description: Detects the rope.pyz collector cmdline patterns used to steal GitHub PATs and decrypt GPG-protected credentials, parented by a python3 process spawned from the durabletask import.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/microsofts-durabletask-pypi-package-compromised-in-supply-chain-attack
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1555
  - attack.t1528
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
  gh_token:
    Image|endswith: '/gh'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'auth token'
      - 'auth status --show-token'
  gpg_anon:
    Image|endswith: '/gpg'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '--batch'
      - '--passphrase anon'
      - '--decrypt'
  condition: parent and (gh_token or gpg_anon)
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.parent.name:(python OR python3) AND ((@process.executable.path:*/gh AND @process.command_line:(*"auth token"* OR *"auth status --show-token"*)) OR (@process.executable.path:*/gpg AND @process.command_line:*"--batch --passphrase anon --decrypt"*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/python3?$/i
| ((ImageFileName=/\/gh$/i AND regex("auth (token|status --show-token)", field=CommandLine)) OR (ImageFileName=/\/gpg$/i AND regex("--batch.*--passphrase\\s+anon.*--decrypt", field=CommandLine)))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count values(Processes.process) as cmd_samples min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="python3" AND ( (Processes.process_name="gh" AND (Processes.process="*auth token*" OR Processes.process="*auth status --show-token*")) OR (Processes.process_name="gpg" AND Processes.process="*--batch --passphrase anon --decrypt*") ) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Processes.process) as cmd_samples min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="python3" AND ( (Processes.process_name="gh" AND (Processes.process="*auth token*" OR Processes.process="*auth status --show-token*")) OR (Processes.process_name="gpg" AND Processes.process="*--batch --passphrase anon --decrypt*") ) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] Fake pgsql-monitor.service systemd persistence written under ~/.config/systemd/user/ Installation High
Detects creation of the article-named `pgsql-monitor.service` user-level systemd unit file, and the follow-up `systemctl --user daemon-reload` spawned by a python3 process — the exact persistence mechanism each of the four managed.pyz collector instances installs. Rationale: Article names the exact persistence artefact (`pgsql-monitor.service`) and the exact cmdline (`systemctl --user daemon-reload`) spawned by each of the four parallel managed.pyz instances. User-level systemd persistence under `~/.config/systemd/user/` is rare on CI runners and cloud-workload base images. No external sources cross-checked.
ATT&CKT1543.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
let file_persist = DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where (FolderPath has "/.config/systemd/user" and FileName endswith ".service")
     or FileName =~ "pgsql-monitor.service"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Signal="FileWrite";
let daemon_reload = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName =~ "systemctl"
  | where ProcessCommandLine has "--user" and ProcessCommandLine has "daemon-reload"
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName="systemctl", FolderPath=ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Signal="DaemonReload";
union file_persist, daemon_reload
| order by Timestamp desc
let file_persist = ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventType in~ ("FileCreated","FileModified")
  | where (TargetFilePath has "/.config/systemd/user" and TargetFileName endswith ".service")
     or TargetFileName =~ "pgsql-monitor.service"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Signal="FileWrite";
let daemon_reload = ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessName =~ "systemctl"
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "--user" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "daemon-reload"
  | where ParentProcessName in~ ("python","python3")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath=ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileName="systemctl", ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine=ParentProcessCommandLine, Signal="DaemonReload";
union file_persist, daemon_reload
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: TeamPCP pgsql-monitor.service Systemd Persistence (durabletask Compromise)
id: 4c2e9f73-86a1-4b2d-b3f8-9e7a4d1c8b25
description: Detects creation of the pgsql-monitor.service user-level systemd unit that rope.pyz installs for persistence, or python3-parented systemctl --user daemon-reload invocations that activate it.

(source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:PATH @file.path:(*/.config/systemd/user/pgsql-monitor.service OR */.config/systemd/user/*.service)) OR (source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.parent.name:(python OR python3) @process.command_line:*"systemctl --user daemon-reload"*)

| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, TargetFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
(`tstats` summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="pgsql-monitor.service" OR (Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/systemd/user/*" AND Filesystem.action="created") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`) | append [| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="systemctl" AND Processes.process="*--user*daemon-reload*" AND Processes.parent_process_name="python3" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
(`tstats` summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="pgsql-monitor.service" OR (Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/systemd/user/*" AND Filesystem.action="created") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`) | append [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="systemctl" AND Processes.process="*--user*daemon-reload*" AND Processes.parent_process_name="python3" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] Burst of AWS SSM SendCommand / StartSession from stolen durabletask credentials Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for the article's lateral-movement pattern: stolen ~/.aws/credentials being used to enumerate SSM-managed instances and run remote commands or shell sessions. Looks for a single IAM principal calling DescribeInstanceInformation followed by SendCommand or StartSession from a fresh source IP within a short window. Rationale: Article confirms `propagates to other machines through AWS SSM and Kubernetes kubectl exec` after harvesting AWS credentials from ~/.aws/credentials. The high-signal pattern is DescribeInstanceInformation immediately followed by SendCommand or StartSession from the same principal within a short window — classic SSM-as-RCE TTP. Hunting tier because legitimate ops engineers do this too. Defender / Sentinel KQL left empty because their canonical schemas in this tenant do not include AWSCloudTrail; the Sentinel column list above contains no AWSCloudTrail table — operators ingesting CloudTrail via the AWS S3 connector would have a `AWSCloudTrail` table not in the canonical schema. No external sources cross-checked.
ATT&CKT1021.007 T1078.004 T1580
Data sourcesAuthentication
source:cloudtrail @evt.name:(DescribeInstanceInformation OR SendCommand OR StartSession OR ResumeSession) @evt.outcome:success @userIdentity.type:(IAMUser OR AssumedRole)
# log group: /aws/cloudtrail
fields @timestamp, eventName, sourceIPAddress, userIdentity.arn, userIdentity.userName, userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName, awsRegion, requestParameters.instanceIds, requestParameters.documentName, requestParameters.target
| filter eventSource = "ssm.amazonaws.com"
      and eventName in ["DescribeInstanceInformation", "SendCommand", "StartSession", "ResumeSession", "GetCommandInvocation"]
      and not isPresent(errorCode)
| stats count(*) as calls, count_distinct(eventName) as event_types, count_distinct(sourceIPAddress) as src_ips, earliest(@timestamp) as first_seen, latest(@timestamp) as last_seen by userIdentity.arn
| filter event_types >= 2
| sort last_seen desc
CLOUD
`cloudtrail` (eventName=DescribeInstanceInformation OR eventName=SendCommand OR eventName=StartSession OR eventName=ResumeSession) errorCode="*" OR errorCode=NULL
| eval principal=coalesce('userIdentity.arn','userIdentity.userName')
| stats earliest(_time) as firstSeen latest(_time) as lastSeen dc(eventName) as eventTypes values(eventName) as events values(sourceIPAddress) as srcIPs dc(sourceIPAddress) as srcIPCount count by principal
| where eventTypes >= 2 AND srcIPCount >= 1
| eval windowSec=lastSeen-firstSeen
| where windowSec <= 1800
| convert ctime(firstSeen) ctime(lastSeen)
| sort - firstSeen
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("160.119.64.3") or RemoteUrl has_any ("t.m-kosche.com", "check.git-service.com", "privacyguardian.org", "ns3.dnsowl.com", "git-service.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["160.119.64.3"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["t.m-kosche.com", "check.git-service.com", "privacyguardian.org", "ns3.dnsowl.com", "git-service.com"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45321")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45321")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-45321")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-45321")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase

    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access

    product: windows

        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'

            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'

        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'

falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

Securing CI/CD in an agentic world: Claude Code Github action case

Microsoft Security Blog
2026-06-05 7 use cases 8 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Microsoft Threat Intelligence identified a prompt injection pathway in Claude Code GitHub Action that allowed access to workflow secrets under specific conditions. This research examines the attack chain, responsible disclosure process, Anthropic's mitigation, and guidance for securing AI-powered CI/CD workflows. The post Securing CI/CD in an agentic world: Claude Code Github action case appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Claude Code Action Read tool exfil: node opens /proc/<pid>/environ on Linux CI runner · [LLM] Claude Code Read tool steered to cloud-credential files on GitHub Actions runner · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] GitHub Actions runner: node from Claude Code Action egresses to non-Anthropic/non-GitHub endpoint
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] Claude Code Action Read tool exfil: node opens /proc/<pid>/environ on Linux CI runner Exploitation High
Hunts the exact exploitation primitive Microsoft Threat Intelligence described: the Claude Code Action's in-process Read tool, when steered by an injected prompt, opens /proc/self/environ (or /proc/<pid>/environ) to harvest the workflow's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, and OIDC credentials. Pre-fix (claude-code-action <2.1.128) the Bubblewrap sandbox + CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB does not cover Read, so the node process serving Claude Code opens /proc directly — a path almost nothing legitimate touches on a build runner. Rationale: Article names the exact primitive: 'eventually authorized to access /proc/self/environ, reading the workflow's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'. We pin on the Linux file path regex + node as the actor. The Read tool runs in-process inside node (not via Bash), so the file event is the only signal — there is no child process to pivot on. Corroborated by Flatt Security (flatt.tech) and Hacker News reporting which describe the same /proc/self/environ exfil chain. Cross-checked against: • https://flatt.tech/research/posts/poisoning-claude-code-one-github-issue-to-break-the-supply-chain/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/claude-code-github-action-flaw-let-one.html • https://oddguan.com/blog/comment-and-control-prompt-injection-credential-theft-claude-code-gemini-cli-github-copilot/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1212 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node"
| where FolderPath matches regex @"^/proc/(self|\d+)/environ$"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("_work/", "actions-runner", "_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action", "runners/") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("@anthropic-ai/claude-code", "claude-code-action")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessId,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "/node" or ActingProcessName =~ "node"
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"^/proc/(self|\d+)/environ$"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("claude-code", "@anthropic-ai", "_actions/anthropics", "actions-runner", "/_work/")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          ActingProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessId, TargetFilePath, EventType, DvcAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Node Process Reads /proc/<pid>/environ on CI Runner (Claude Code Action Read Tool Exfil)
id: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4789-9abc-def012345678
description: Detects Node.js opening /proc/self/environ or /proc/<pid>/environ on Linux hosts. Microsoft Threat Intelligence flagged this as the exfiltration primitive that lets a prompt-injected Claude Code GitHub Action steal ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/GITHUB_TOKEN/OIDC creds from the workflow environment (fixed in claude-code-action 2.1.128).
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/05/securing-ci-cd-in-agentic-world-claude-code-github-action-case/
  - https://flatt.tech/research/posts/poisoning-claude-code-one-github-issue-to-break-the-supply-chain/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1212
logsource:
  category: file_access
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith: '/node'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|re: '^/proc/(self|\d+)/environ$'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_path
falsepositives:
  - Process inspection / observability agents (e.g. Datadog process-agent, sysdig) running as node
  - Self-introspection by a Node tool reading its OWN /proc/self/environ for debugging (rare in CI)
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:(SYSCALL OR PATH) (@process.name:node OR @process.executable.path:*/node) (@file.path:/proc/self/environ OR @file.path:/proc/*/environ)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo ContextImageFileName=/\/node$/i TargetFileName=/^\/proc\/(self|\d+)\/environ$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId, TargetFileName], function=count(as=opens, distinct=false))
| opens > 0

[LLM] Claude Code Read tool steered to cloud-credential files on GitHub Actions runner Exploitation Medium
Even after the /proc fix in claude-code-action 2.1.128, an attacker who controls the prompt can still steer the Read tool to any path the runner can see. This hunts node — running from the Actions work dir — opening the common secret stores a CI job tends to have on disk: ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc (NPM publish token), ~/.docker/config.json (registry token), ~/.kube/config, ~/.netrc, SSH keys, .env files. Microsoft's article explicitly calls out that 'once an attacker can influence the agent, they might be able to steer it toward sensitive files available inside the CI runner environment'. Rationale: Article: 'once an attacker can influence the agent, they might be able to steer it toward sensitive files available inside the CI runner environment.' We restrict to node spawned from `_work/` or the anthropic action checkout dir so legit user shell activity reading `~/.aws/credentials` doesn't fire. Path list is the GitHub Actions secret canon — npm publish tokens, docker registry creds, GitHub CLI tokens, terraform/pypi publishers — all of which routinely live in runner home dirs. Cross-checked: Flatt's writeup confirms ANTHROPIC_API_KEY + GITHUB_TOKEN + OIDC creds are the named targets, the broader hunt covers what would be next. Cross-checked against: • https://flatt.tech/research/posts/poisoning-claude-code-one-github-issue-to-break-the-supply-chain/ • https://oddguan.com/blog/comment-and-control-prompt-injection-credential-theft-claude-code-gemini-cli-github-copilot/

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("_work/", "actions-runner", "_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action") 
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("@anthropic-ai/claude-code", "claude-code-action")
| where FolderPath has_any (CredPaths)
   or FolderPath matches regex @"\.ssh/id_(rsa|ed25519|dsa|ecdsa)$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessId,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let CredPaths = dynamic([".aws/credentials", ".npmrc", ".gitconfig", ".docker/config.json", ".kube/config", ".netrc", "/.env", ".config/gh/hosts.yml", ".terraformrc", ".pypirc"]);

title: Claude Code Read Tool Accessing Credential Files on GitHub Actions Runner
id: b2c3d4e5-f6a7-4890-9bcd-ef0123456789
description: Node.js (running Claude Code Action or the Anthropic SDK) opening common credential / token files on a Linux GitHub Actions runner. Catches Read-tool abuse beyond the patched /proc primitive — an attacker who controls the AI prompt can still steer Read at ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.docker/config.json, SSH keys, and .env.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/05/securing-ci-cd-in-agentic-world-claude-code-github-action-case/
  - https://flatt.tech/research/posts/poisoning-claude-code-one-github-issue-to-break-the-supply-chain/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1552.004
logsource:
  category: file_access
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith: '/node'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '/.aws/credentials'
      - '/.npmrc'
      - '/.gitconfig'
      - '/.docker/config.json'
      - '/.kube/config'
      - '/.netrc'
      - '/.config/gh/hosts.yml'
      - '/.terraformrc'
      - '/.pypirc'
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '/.env'
  selection_ssh:
    TargetFilename|re: '/\.ssh/id_(rsa|ed25519|dsa|ecdsa)$'
  condition: selection_proc and (selection_path or selection_ssh)
falsepositives:
  - Genuine CI jobs that legitimately use these credentials (build step reading .npmrc to publish, terraform reading .aws/credentials). Refine by parent-process / runner identity.
level: high

[LLM] GitHub Actions runner: node from Claude Code Action egresses to non-Anthropic/non-GitHub endpoint Command & Control Medium
Closes the loop on the exfiltration step. The Claude Code Action's legitimate outbound destinations are tightly scoped — api.anthropic.com (LLM calls) and the GitHub control plane (api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, ghcr.io, results-receiver.actions.githubusercontent.com). When the same node process under `_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action` reaches anything else on a public IP, an attacker is probably steering it to POST the stolen ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OIDC token to their collection endpoint, or to fetch a second-stage payload to plant into a PR (the docs-XSS scenario from Figure 1). Rationale: Article's threat model is clear: 'the workflow's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and potentially other credentials available to the runner' get exfiltrated, and the same agent primitive 'create_pull_request_from_changes' lets the attacker reach an external endpoint to receive them or fetch payloads. Allowlist is built from Anthropic's API host plus the GitHub Actions runtime control-plane domains (the only IPs a legit claude-code-action job needs). Anything else from a node process under `_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action` is suspicious by construction. No Sigma — needs cross-table join (process attribution + network destination + DNS). Cross-checked against: • https://flatt.tech/research/posts/poisoning-claude-code-one-github-issue-to-break-the-supply-chain/ • https://www.securityweek.com/claude-code-gemini-cli-github-copilot-agents-vulnerable-to-prompt-injection-via-comments/
ATT&CKT1041 T1071.001 T1567
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
let RunnerNode = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName =~ "node"
    | where FolderPath has_any ("_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action", "_work/", "actions-runner")
         or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("@anthropic-ai/claude-code", "claude-code-action")
    | project NodeTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, NodePid = ProcessId, NodeCmd = ProcessCommandLine, NodeFolder = FolderPath;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where not(RemoteUrl has_any ("anthropic.com", "api.github.com", "githubusercontent.com", "githubapp.com", "githubassets.com", "ghcr.io", "actions.githubusercontent.com"))
| where isnotempty(RemoteIP)
| join kind=inner RunnerNode on $left.DeviceId == $right.DeviceId, $left.InitiatingProcessId == $right.NodePid
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, NodeCmd, NodeFolder, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| summarize HitCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), Destinations = make_set(RemoteUrl, 20), DestIPs = make_set(RemoteIP, 20)
           by DeviceName, NodeFolder, RemotePort
| order by FirstSeen desc
let AllowList = dynamic(["anthropic.com", "api.github.com", "githubusercontent.com", "githubapp.com", "githubassets.com", "ghcr.io", "actions.githubusercontent.com"]);
let RunnerHosts = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName endswith "/node" or TargetProcessName endswith "/node"
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action", "@anthropic-ai/claude-code", "claude-code-action", "/_work/")
    | distinct DvcHostname;
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DvcHostname in (RunnerHosts)
| where isnotempty(DstHostname)
| where DstIpAddr !startswith "10." and DstIpAddr !startswith "192.168." 
     and not(DstIpAddr matches regex @"^172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.") 
     and DstIpAddr !startswith "127." and DstIpAddr !startswith "169.254."
| where not(DstHostname has_any (AllowList))
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), HitCount = count(), SampleUrl = any(Url)
           by DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol
| order by FirstSeen desc
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 OR source:linux.auditd) (@process.name:node OR @process.executable.path:*/node) (@ParentImage:*claude-code* OR @process.command_line:*claude-code* OR @process.command_line:*@anthropic-ai*) NOT (@DestinationHostname:*.anthropic.com OR @DestinationHostname:*.github.com OR @DestinationHostname:*.githubusercontent.com OR @DestinationHostname:*.ghcr.io OR @DestinationHostname:*.githubapp.com OR @DestinationHostname:*.githubassets.com) NOT CIDR(@network.destination.ip, 10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.0.0/16, 172.16.0.0/12, 127.0.0.0/8, 169.254.0.0/16)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ContextImageFileName=/\/node$/i
| regex("(actions-runner|_work|_actions\\/anthropics\\/claude-code-action)", field=ContextImageFileName, strict=false)
| RemoteAddressIP4!=/^(10\.|192\.168\.|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.|127\.|169\.254\.)/
| join({#event_simpleName=DnsRequest | DomainName!=/(anthropic\.com|github\.com|githubusercontent\.com|ghcr\.io|githubapp\.com|githubassets\.com)$/i | groupBy([aid, FirstIP4Record], function=collect(DomainName, as=resolved_domain))}, field=[aid, RemoteAddressIP4=FirstIP4Record])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort, resolved_domain], function=count(as=conns))
| conns > 0

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

[LLM] DbGate Zip Slip (CVE-2026-47669): node process writes outside archive dir to OS-sensitive paths Installation High
Detects the Zip Slip exploitation outcome of CVE-2026-47669 where the DbGate node process — invoked via /api/archive/unzip — writes files to OS-sensitive Linux paths (cron, sudoers, SSH authorized_keys, ld.so.preload, systemd units, /usr/local/bin) via `../` entries in a malicious ZIP. In a clean DbGate deployment the node process should only write inside its archive directory, so any write under /etc, /root/.ssh, or /usr/local/bin from node is high-fidelity for this CVE. Rationale: Pivots on the EXACT Zip Slip exploit outcome described in the GHSA PoC: `path.join(outputDirectory, entry.fileName)` allows `../` traversal, and the PoC writes to `/etc/cron.d/dbgate-pwn`. The dbgate node process has no legitimate reason to touch /etc/cron.*, /etc/sudoers.d, /root/.ssh, /etc/ld.so.preload, or /usr/local/bin — these are the canonical persistence/privesc paths attackers traverse to. Corroborated against Snyk's prior DbGate Zip Slip advisory which confirms the same vulnerable archive-extraction code path. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h535-j5hr-mv56 • https://security.snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-JS-DBGATEAPI-11023274
ATT&CKT1190 T1053.003 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
// CVE-2026-47669 DbGate Zip Slip - node process writes outside archive dir
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("dbgate", "packages/api", "/app/packages")
| where FolderPath startswith "/etc/cron." 
    or FolderPath startswith "/var/spool/cron/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/etc/sudoers.d/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/root/.ssh/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/etc/init.d/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/etc/profile.d/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/etc/systemd/system/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/usr/local/bin/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/usr/local/sbin/"
    or FolderPath == "/etc/ld.so.preload"
    or FolderPath == "/etc/passwd"
    or FolderPath == "/etc/shadow"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-47669 DbGate Zip Slip - ASIM ImFileEvent (covers MDE for Linux + Sysmon for Linux + auditd)
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "/node" or ActingProcessName =~ "node"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("dbgate", "packages/api", "/app/packages")
| where TargetFilePath startswith "/etc/cron."
    or TargetFilePath startswith "/var/spool/cron/"
    or TargetFilePath startswith "/etc/sudoers.d/"
    or TargetFilePath startswith "/root/.ssh/"
    or TargetFilePath startswith "/etc/init.d/"
    or TargetFilePath startswith "/etc/profile.d/"
    or TargetFilePath startswith "/etc/systemd/system/"
    or TargetFilePath startswith "/usr/local/bin/"
    or TargetFilePath startswith "/usr/local/sbin/"
    or TargetFilePath in ("/etc/ld.so.preload","/etc/passwd","/etc/shadow")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName,
          TargetFileSHA256, EventType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: DbGate Zip Slip (CVE-2026-47669) - Node Writes to OS-Sensitive Linux Paths
id: 7c9a4a16-2c4f-4c2c-9b1a-2026476690a1
description: Detects the DbGate node process writing files to OS-sensitive Linux paths (cron, sudoers.d, /root/.ssh, ld.so.preload, systemd units, /usr/local/bin) via the Zip Slip vulnerability in unzipDirectory.js. In a normal DbGate deployment node should only write under its archive directory.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h535-j5hr-mv56
  - https://security.snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-JS-DBGATEAPI-11023274
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1053.003
  - attack.t1505.003
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.persistence
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
detection:
  proc:
    Image|endswith: '/node'
  cmdline_dbgate:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'dbgate'
      - 'packages/api'
  target_paths_prefix:
    TargetFilename|startswith:
      - '/etc/cron.d/'
      - '/etc/cron.daily/'
      - '/etc/cron.hourly/'
      - '/etc/cron.weekly/'
      - '/etc/cron.monthly/'
      - '/var/spool/cron/'
      - '/etc/sudoers.d/'
      - '/root/.ssh/'
      - '/etc/init.d/'
      - '/etc/profile.d/'
      - '/etc/systemd/system/'
      - '/usr/local/bin/'
      - '/usr/local/sbin/'
  target_paths_exact:
    TargetFilename:
      - '/etc/ld.so.preload'
      - '/etc/passwd'
      - '/etc/shadow'
  condition: proc and cmdline_dbgate and (target_paths_prefix or target_paths_exact)
level: critical
(source:linux.auditd OR source:windows.sysmon) @process.name:node @process.command_line:(*dbgate* OR *packages\/api*) @file.path:("/etc/cron.d/*" OR "/etc/cron.daily/*" OR "/etc/cron.hourly/*" OR "/var/spool/cron/*" OR "/etc/sudoers.d/*" OR "/root/.ssh/*" OR "/etc/init.d/*" OR "/etc/profile.d/*" OR "/etc/systemd/system/*" OR "/usr/local/bin/*" OR "/usr/local/sbin/*" OR "/etc/ld.so.preload" OR "/etc/passwd" OR "/etc/shadow")
#event_simpleName=FileWritten ContextImageFileName=/\/node$/i
| regex("(dbgate|packages\\/api)", field=ContextCommandLine, strict=false)
| regex("^(\\/etc\\/cron\\.(d|daily|hourly|weekly|monthly)\\/|\\/var\\/spool\\/cron\\/|\\/etc\\/sudoers\\.d\\/|\\/root\\/\\.ssh\\/|\\/etc\\/init\\.d\\/|\\/etc\\/profile\\.d\\/|\\/etc\\/systemd\\/system\\/|\\/usr\\/local\\/(bin|sbin)\\/|\\/etc\\/ld\\.so\\.preload$|\\/etc\\/passwd$|\\/etc\\/shadow$)", field=TargetFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName, UserName], function=count())

[LLM] DbGate exploit chain: anonymous /auth/login + /api/archive/unzip POSTs from same source (CVE-2026-47669) Exploitation Medium
Detects the multi-step exploit sequence against DbGate's vulnerable archive endpoints: POST /api/auth/login (no creds via amoid=none), POST /api/uploads/upload, POST /api/archive/save-uploaded-zip, POST /api/archive/unzip — all hit by the same source IP within a short window. This is the network-edge view of CVE-2026-47669 exploitation, complementary to host-side file-write detection. Rationale: Targets the EXACT URL set in the PoC (POST /api/auth/login with amoid=none, /api/uploads/upload, /api/archive/save-uploaded-zip, /api/archive/unzip). The chain of >=2 distinct endpoints including unzip or save-uploaded-zip from one source IP is the network-shape of the exploit. Defender/Falcon left empty because neither has inbound HTTP request-URL visibility for DbGate's port. Corroborated via Snyk advisory for the prior dbgate-api Zip Slip variant. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h535-j5hr-mv56 • https://security.snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-JS-DBGATEAPI-11023274
ATT&CKT1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb
// CVE-2026-47669 DbGate exploit chain via WAF/proxy logs in CommonSecurityLog
let ExploitEndpoints = dynamic(["/api/archive/unzip","/api/archive/save-uploaded-zip","/api/uploads/upload","/api/auth/login"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
| where RequestURL has_any (ExploitEndpoints)
| extend Endpoint = case(
    RequestURL has "/api/archive/unzip", "unzip",
    RequestURL has "/api/archive/save-uploaded-zip", "save-uploaded-zip",
    RequestURL has "/api/uploads/upload", "upload",
    RequestURL has "/api/auth/login", "login",
    "other")
| summarize EndpointsHit = make_set(Endpoint),
            UrlSamples = make_set(RequestURL, 10),
            UASet = make_set(RequestClientApplication),
            ReqCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by SourceIP, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP
| where array_length(EndpointsHit) >= 2
    and (set_has_element(EndpointsHit, "unzip") or set_has_element(EndpointsHit, "save-uploaded-zip"))
| order by LastSeen desc

[LLM] DbGate CVE-2026-47668 — Node.js runner spawning shell/LOLBin children for egress Exploitation High
Detects exploitation of DbGate's JSON Script Runner RCE where attacker-injected JavaScript in the `functionName` parameter calls `process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync()` to launch shell utilities (wget/curl/sh/bash/powershell) from the forked dbgate runner Node.js process. Targets the exploit chain post-injection where the spawned child commands betray the RCE. Rationale: Pins to the exact post-exploit footprint described in the advisory: the forked Node.js runner (working dir `/root/.dbgate/run/<uuid>`, env `DBGATE_API=/home/dbgate-docker/bundle.js`) executing shell utilities via `child_process.execSync()` — concretely `wget --post-data "$(env)"` in the PoC. Parent-cmdline anchors (`bundle.js`, `.dbgate/run/`, `dbgate-docker`) are dbgate-specific artifacts not present in benign Node workloads.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1059.007

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("bundle.js",".dbgate/run/","dbgate-docker","DBGATE_API")
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/home/dbgate-docker","\\dbgate\\","/.dbgate/run/")
| where FileName in~ ("wget","curl","sh","bash","dash","zsh","powershell.exe","pwsh","cmd.exe","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl","ruby","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,

[LLM] DbGate exploit web request — POST /runners/start or /runners/load-reader with child_process injection Delivery High
Detects HTTP exploitation traffic for CVE-2026-47668 in reverse-proxy / WAF / IIS / web-server access logs: POST requests to DbGate's `/runners/start` or `/runners/load-reader` endpoints, optionally paired with body inspection matching the JS injection signatures (`process.mainModule.require`, `child_process`, `execSync`, `module.constructor._load`). Aims at the network-side of the exploit before payload execution. Rationale: Endpoint paths `/runners/start` and `/runners/load-reader` are advisory-specific (not generic API hits) and the runner endpoints are not part of any user-browser flow — any POST to them from outside curated automation is suspicious. Cross-join with the host-side process spike (forked node runner) elevates signal further.

[LLM] DbGate anonymous auth-bypass token mint — POST /auth/login with amoid:none Reconnaissance Medium
Detects the precursor to CVE-2026-47668 exploitation against a default-deployed DbGate: an unauthenticated `POST /auth/login` carrying body `{"amoid":"none"}` to mint a bearer token when `authProvider:"Anonymous"` (the default). Captures recon/auth-prep traffic that almost always precedes the runner-endpoint hit. Rationale: The advisory documents the exact unauth token-mint vector — `curl -d '{"amoid":"none"}' <dbgate>:3000/auth/login` — used when `authProvider` is left at its default `Anonymous`. Pairing the `/auth/login` POST with a following `/runners/start` or `/runners/load-reader` from the same source within 30 minutes is the full exploit handshake.
ATT&CKT1078.001 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let auth =
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where RequestMethod == "POST" and RequestURL has "/auth/login"
    | project AuthTime=TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication;
let runner =
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where RequestMethod == "POST" and RequestURL has_any ("/runners/start","/runners/load-reader")
    | project RunTime=TimeGenerated, SourceIP, RequestURL_Runner=RequestURL;
auth
| join kind=inner runner on SourceIP
| where RunTime between (AuthTime .. AuthTime + 30m)
| project AuthTime, RunTime, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL_Runner, RequestClientApplication
| order by AuthTime desc

[LLM] PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 GlobalProtect login from Unit 42 IOC IPs Exploitation High
Hunt for successful GlobalProtect gateway-connected events sourced from the nine IP addresses Unit 42 attributes to pre-PoC CVE-2026-0257 exploitation. Any successful VPN session from one of these IPs is a high-confidence compromise indicator since the article confirms the actor uses them to bypass GP portal/gateway authentication. Rationale: Uses the nine attacker-IP IOCs published by Unit 42 in the CVE-2026-0257 threat brief — explicit, vendor-attributed, and tied to a CISA KEV-listed exploitation campaign. Matched against PAN-OS GlobalProtect login telemetry which is the exact telemetry the article tells defenders to search. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/

[LLM] PAN-OS GlobalProtect login with CVE-2026-0257 PoC hard-coded host-id / device-name Exploitation High
Hunt for GlobalProtect gateway-connected events whose host-id or device name matches the hard-coded values shipped in the public CVE-2026-0257 PoC code. These strings appear in the GP client-info payload sent during the auth-bypass and are not naturally generated by real corporate endpoints. Rationale: The Unit 42 brief explicitly names these MAC and machine-name strings as defaults baked into the published PoC code — they are the cleanest unique fingerprint of attacker traffic vs legitimate VPN clients. These would rarely if ever appear in a real corporate environment, so the FP rate is near-zero. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/

[LLM] PAN-OS GlobalProtect login matching CVE-2026-0257 PoC client fingerprint Exploitation High
Hunt for GP gateway-connected events carrying the hard-coded endpoint_os_version 'Microsoft Windows 10 Pro 64-bit' AND an empty source_user_info.domain — the exact post-PoC release fingerprint Unit 42 documents in the threat brief. Legitimate clients fill in the joined domain; the PoC leaves it blank. Rationale: Unit 42 explicitly publishes endpoint_os_version='Microsoft Windows 10 Pro 64-bit' + empty source_user_info.domain as the post-PoC client fingerprint of the CVE-2026-0257 exploit. The empty-domain clause is what shifts it from common-OS noise into high-fidelity exploit signal — real corporate GP clients almost always populate that field with the AD domain. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
// PAN-OS GP client-info strings do not flow into Defender XDR natively.
// Where GP logs are ingested via a custom MDE connector, the substring lives in AdditionalFields:
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType has "GlobalProtect"
| where AdditionalFields has "Microsoft Windows 10 Pro 64-bit"
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("source_user_info.domain=\"\"","source_user_info.domain=null","\"domain\":\"\"")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, AccountName, AdditionalFields
CommonSecurityLog

| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, SourceUserName, SourceNTDomain, SourceHostName, DeviceAction, Activity, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-0257")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-0257")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High

DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"

| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT

    Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore files from MetaMask,
    Exodus, Atomic, Phantom, Bitcoin, Electrum, Ethereum-cli wallets.
    Filtering out the legitimate wallet binaries leaves only attacker
    activity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1005/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1005
    - attack.collection
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Ethereum\keystore\'
            - '\Bitcoin\'
            - '\Exodus\'
            - '\Electrum\wallets\'
            - '\MetaMask\'
            - '\Phantom\'
            - '\Atomic\Local Storage\'
    filter_legit:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\MetaMask.exe'
            - '\Exodus.exe'
            - '\Atomic.exe'
            - '\electrum.exe'
            - '\Bitcoin.exe'
            - '\Phantom.exe'
    condition: selection_path and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
    - Backup software
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6552824c59ddacb134073f24a4bd4724514a938a9dc59f1733503642faed3bd3", "c917fcf8314228862571f80c9e4a871e") or SHA1 in~ ("6552824c59ddacb134073f24a4bd4724514a938a9dc59f1733503642faed3bd3", "c917fcf8314228862571f80c9e4a871e") or MD5 in~ ("6552824c59ddacb134073f24a4bd4724514a938a9dc59f1733503642faed3bd3", "c917fcf8314228862571f80c9e4a871e")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6552824c59ddacb134073f24a4bd4724514a938a9dc59f1733503642faed3bd3", "c917fcf8314228862571f80c9e4a871e") or SHA1 in~ ("6552824c59ddacb134073f24a4bd4724514a938a9dc59f1733503642faed3bd3", "c917fcf8314228862571f80c9e4a871e") or MD5 in~ ("6552824c59ddacb134073f24a4bd4724514a938a9dc59f1733503642faed3bd3", "c917fcf8314228862571f80c9e4a871e")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["6552824c59ddacb134073f24a4bd4724514a938a9dc59f1733503642faed3bd3", "c917fcf8314228862571f80c9e4a871e"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Suspicious browser extension installation · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
