DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any ("\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\","\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\","\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey,
          RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Browser Extension Installation via Registry
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0a
status: experimental
description: |
    Registry writes under the browser extension policy keys —
    administrative install of an extension. Often used by adware /
    info-stealers to bypass user-level extension controls.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1176/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1176
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    category: registry_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetObject|contains:
            - '\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\'
            - '\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\'
            - '\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Group-policy-managed extension whitelists
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
    where (Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")
    by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
    where (Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")
    by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("524c953e23ff8b768206cf33a529c11ac5510e47cbf6246db79ee671d1231716", "c984787ccd787629542da68302ed4ceb48fc7e458eab1c15bf45c3070883d26a", "f8cbe44fde6914bc8d06426c03c92ed536c891470292e567a586b54af29c2442") or SHA1 in~ ("524c953e23ff8b768206cf33a529c11ac5510e47cbf6246db79ee671d1231716", "c984787ccd787629542da68302ed4ceb48fc7e458eab1c15bf45c3070883d26a", "f8cbe44fde6914bc8d06426c03c92ed536c891470292e567a586b54af29c2442") or MD5 in~ ("524c953e23ff8b768206cf33a529c11ac5510e47cbf6246db79ee671d1231716", "c984787ccd787629542da68302ed4ceb48fc7e458eab1c15bf45c3070883d26a", "f8cbe44fde6914bc8d06426c03c92ed536c891470292e567a586b54af29c2442")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("524c953e23ff8b768206cf33a529c11ac5510e47cbf6246db79ee671d1231716", "c984787ccd787629542da68302ed4ceb48fc7e458eab1c15bf45c3070883d26a", "f8cbe44fde6914bc8d06426c03c92ed536c891470292e567a586b54af29c2442") or SHA1 in~ ("524c953e23ff8b768206cf33a529c11ac5510e47cbf6246db79ee671d1231716", "c984787ccd787629542da68302ed4ceb48fc7e458eab1c15bf45c3070883d26a", "f8cbe44fde6914bc8d06426c03c92ed536c891470292e567a586b54af29c2442") or MD5 in~ ("524c953e23ff8b768206cf33a529c11ac5510e47cbf6246db79ee671d1231716", "c984787ccd787629542da68302ed4ceb48fc7e458eab1c15bf45c3070883d26a", "f8cbe44fde6914bc8d06426c03c92ed536c891470292e567a586b54af29c2442")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["524c953e23ff8b768206cf33a529c11ac5510e47cbf6246db79ee671d1231716", "c984787ccd787629542da68302ed4ceb48fc7e458eab1c15bf45c3070883d26a", "f8cbe44fde6914bc8d06426c03c92ed536c891470292e567a586b54af29c2442"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

New Threat Cluster OP-512 Targets Microsoft IIS Servers with Custom Web Shell Framework

The Hacker News
2026-06-05 11 use cases 5 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Cybersecurity researchers have discovered a previously unreported threat cluster dubbed OP-512 (where "OP" stands for "opponent") that has been observed&nbsp;targeting Microsoft Internet Information Services (IIS) servers to deploy a bespoke web shell framework. ReliaQuest has assessed with moderate to high confidence that the espionage-focused activity is linked to China. "OP-512 was highly

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] OP-512 Potato Suite SYSTEM escalation from IIS worker (SeImpersonate token abuse) · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — New Threat Cluster OP-512 Targets Microsoft IIS Servers with Custom Web Shell Fr
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] IIS worker w3wp.exe writes .aspx/.ashx handler to upload/temp directory (OP-512 web shell drop)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] OP-512 C2 beacon to ashx.lhlsjcb[.]com from IIS host · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] IIS w3wp.exe spawns whoami /priv or cmd.exe — OP-512 web shell command execution · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] OP-512 C2 beacon to ashx.lhlsjcb[.]com from IIS host Command & Control High
Detects DNS resolutions or HTTP egress to the OP-512 attacker-controlled domain ashx.lhlsjcb[.]com observed in the ReliaQuest report. Article-specific because this domain appeared ~75 days before the main intrusion as the initial staging beacon and is reused by the web shell's self-reporting fallback over DNS/HTTP. Rationale: The domain ashx.lhlsjcb[.]com is the only network IOC named in the ReliaQuest write-up; matching it across DNS and HTTP egress is a definitive OP-512 signal. Cross-checked the IOC pattern via the article's lead and MITRE T1071.004 mapping. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/004/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where RemoteUrl has "lhlsjcb.com" or RemoteUrl has_cs "ashx.lhlsjcb.com"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp asc
let ioc_domain = "lhlsjcb.com";
(union isfuzzy=true
    (DnsEvents
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
        | where Name has ioc_domain
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, ClientIP, Domain = Name, QueryTypeName, Source = "DnsEvents"),
    (ImDnsActivity
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
        | where DnsQuery has ioc_domain
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, ClientIP = SrcIpAddr, Domain = DnsQuery, QueryTypeName = DnsQueryTypeName, Source = "ImDnsActivity"),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
        | where RequestURL has ioc_domain or DestinationHostName has ioc_domain or DestinationDnsDomain has ioc_domain
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = SourceHostName, ClientIP = SourceIP, Domain = coalesce(DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain), URL = RequestURL, Source = "CommonSecurityLog")
)
| order by TimeGenerated asc

[LLM] IIS worker w3wp.exe writes .aspx/.ashx handler to upload/temp directory (OP-512 web shell drop) Installation High
Detects the IIS worker process w3wp.exe writing ASP.NET handler files (.aspx, .ashx, .asmx) into upload or temp directories — the exact drop pattern ReliaQuest observed for the OP-512 three-shell framework. Combines parent-process (w3wp.exe) and target-extension predicates to keep false positives down on legitimate deployment activity. Rationale: ReliaQuest explicitly names w3wp.exe as the process that dropped the web shell into the application's upload directory. The parent (w3wp.exe) + extension (.aspx/.ashx) + path (upload/temp) triple gives strong specificity to OP-512 vs legitimate publish flows. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where FileName endswith ".aspx" or FileName endswith ".ashx" or FileName endswith ".asmx" or FileName endswith ".asax"
| where FolderPath has_any ("\\upload", "\\uploads", "\\temp", "\\tmp", "\\App_Data", "\\images", "\\files")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RequestSourceIP
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has "w3wp.exe"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("aspx", "ashx", "asmx", "asax")
   or TargetFileName endswith ".aspx"
   or TargetFileName endswith ".ashx"
   or TargetFileName endswith ".asmx"
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("\\upload", "\\uploads", "\\temp", "\\tmp", "\\App_Data", "\\images", "\\files")
| project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: IIS w3wp.exe Writes ASP.NET Handler to Upload or Temp Directory
id: 8a2e5d11-7b40-4c5b-9f8a-3d5b6e0c8e21
description: Detects the IIS worker process w3wp.exe creating ASP.NET handler files (.aspx/.ashx/.asmx/.asax) in upload, temp, or App_Data directories — the OP-512 web shell drop pattern.
references:
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-threat-cluster-op-512-targets.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
    - attack.t1505.003
    - attack.t1190
logsource:
    category: file_event
    product: windows
status: experimental
detection:
    selection_proc:
        Image|endswith: '\w3wp.exe'
    selection_ext:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '.aspx'
            - '.ashx'
            - '.asmx'
            - '.asax'
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\upload'
            - '\uploads'
            - '\temp'
            - '\tmp'
            - '\App_Data'
            - '\images'
            - '\files'
    condition: selection_proc and selection_ext and selection_path
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate ASP.NET application publishing via web-deploy through the worker process (rare)
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\w3wp.exe OR *\W3WP.EXE OR *\W3wp.exe) @TargetFilename:(*.aspx OR *.ashx OR *.asmx OR *.asax OR *.ASPX OR *.ASHX) @TargetFilename:(*\upload* OR *\Upload* OR *\UPLOAD* OR *\temp* OR *\Temp* OR *\TEMP* OR *\App_Data* OR *\images* OR *\files*)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| ContextImageFileName=/\\w3wp\.exe$/i
| TargetFileName=/\.(aspx|ashx|asmx|asax)$/i
| regex("\\\\(upload[s]?|temp|tmp|App_Data|images|files)\\\\", field=TargetFileName, flags="i")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=[count(), min(@timestamp)])
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name="w3wp.exe" (Filesystem.file_name="*.aspx" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.ashx" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.asmx" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.asax") (Filesystem.file_path="*\\upload*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\uploads*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\temp*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\tmp*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\App_Data*") by host Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name="w3wp.exe" (Filesystem.file_name="*.aspx" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.ashx" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.asmx" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.asax") (Filesystem.file_path="*\\upload*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\uploads*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\temp*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\tmp*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\App_Data*") by host Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] IIS w3wp.exe spawns whoami /priv or cmd.exe — OP-512 web shell command execution Actions on Objectives High
Detects the IIS worker w3wp.exe spawning interpreter or reconnaissance binaries (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, whoami.exe, net.exe) — directly matching ReliaQuest's observed OP-512 post-exploitation step of running whoami /priv from the web shell to confirm SYSTEM-level privileges after Potato Suite escalation. Rationale: ReliaQuest directly cites whoami /priv as the post-Potato verification command from OP-512, and the entire chain hinges on w3wp.exe being the parent. Parent (w3wp.exe) + child (recon binaries) is exactly the article's described observed sequence. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1033/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1059.003 T1033 T1087
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "whoami.exe", "net.exe", "net1.exe", "systeminfo.exe", "ipconfig.exe", "tasklist.exe", "hostname.exe", "wmic.exe", "reg.exe", "sc.exe")
| extend IsWhoamiPriv = (FileName =~ "whoami.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/priv", "/all", "/groups"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, IsWhoamiPriv
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\w3wp.exe"
| extend ChildName = tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1])
| where ChildName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "whoami.exe", "net.exe", "net1.exe", "systeminfo.exe", "ipconfig.exe", "tasklist.exe", "hostname.exe", "wmic.exe", "reg.exe", "sc.exe")
| extend IsWhoamiPriv = (ChildName =~ "whoami.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("/priv", "/all", "/groups"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType, IsWhoamiPriv
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: IIS Worker w3wp.exe Spawns Recon Binary (OP-512)
id: 4f7b3c6a-2d11-4f8d-8a51-7e2b1a4c9e3f
description: Detects w3wp.exe spawning cmd/powershell/whoami/net/systeminfo as a child, consistent with OP-512 web shell post-exploitation reconnaissance after Potato Suite SYSTEM escalation.
references:
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-threat-cluster-op-512-targets.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
    - attack.t1505.003
    - attack.t1059.003
    - attack.t1033
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
status: experimental
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith: '\w3wp.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\whoami.exe'
            - '\net.exe'
            - '\net1.exe'
            - '\systeminfo.exe'
            - '\ipconfig.exe'
            - '\tasklist.exe'
            - '\hostname.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\reg.exe'
            - '\sc.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - IIS web apps that legitimately shell out to net.exe / ipconfig.exe for diagnostics endpoints (rare)
level: high
source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) (@EventID:4688 OR @EventID:1) @ParentImage:(*\w3wp.exe OR *\W3WP.EXE) @Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\CMD.EXE OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\whoami.exe OR *\WHOAMI.EXE OR *\net.exe OR *\net1.exe OR *\systeminfo.exe OR *\ipconfig.exe OR *\tasklist.exe OR *\hostname.exe OR *\wmic.exe OR *\reg.exe OR *\sc.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^w3wp\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|whoami|net1?|systeminfo|ipconfig|tasklist|hostname|wmic|reg|sc)\.exe$/i
| WhoamiPriv := if(ImageFileName=/whoami\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/\/(priv|all|groups)/i, "true", "false")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=[count(), min(@timestamp)])
ENDPOINT

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="w3wp.exe" (Processes.process_name="cmd.exe" OR Processes.process_name="powershell.exe" OR Processes.process_name="pwsh.exe" OR Processes.process_name="whoami.exe" OR Processes.process_name="net.exe" OR Processes.process_name="net1.exe" OR Processes.process_name="systeminfo.exe" OR Processes.process_name="ipconfig.exe" OR Processes.process_name="tasklist.exe" OR Processes.process_name="hostname.exe") by host Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="w3wp.exe" (Processes.process_name="cmd.exe" OR Processes.process_name="powershell.exe" OR Processes.process_name="pwsh.exe" OR Processes.process_name="whoami.exe" OR Processes.process_name="net.exe" OR Processes.process_name="net1.exe" OR Processes.process_name="systeminfo.exe" OR Processes.process_name="ipconfig.exe" OR Processes.process_name="tasklist.exe" OR Processes.process_name="hostname.exe") by host Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] OP-512 Potato Suite SYSTEM escalation from IIS worker (SeImpersonate token abuse) Exploitation High
Detects token-impersonation privilege escalation from the IIS app-pool identity to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM — the exact Potato Suite (RottenPotato/JuicyPotato/GodPotato/RoguePotato) chain ReliaQuest observed after OP-512 dropped its web shells. Pivots on child of w3wp.exe with integrity-level jump to System, plus Windows 4672 'special privileges' assignments to non-service accounts. Rationale: ReliaQuest explicitly names the Potato Suite as OP-512's escalation tool from the IIS app-pool to SYSTEM. The IIS-worker-as-parent plus Potato binary-name keywords plus integrity-level jump make this a high-fidelity escalation indicator. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1134/001/ • https://github.com/ohpe/juicy-potato • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/
ATT&CKT1134.001 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let PotatoFingerprints = dynamic(["juicypotato", "rottenpotato", "sweetpotato", "godpotato", "roguepotato", "localpotato", "remotepotato", "printspoofer", "efspotato"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where ProcessIntegrityLevel in~ ("System", "High")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any (PotatoFingerprints)
   or FileName has_any (PotatoFingerprints)
   or InitiatingProcessTokenElevation =~ "TokenElevationTypeFull" and AccountName =~ "SYSTEM" and InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("system", "network service", "local service")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessIntegrityLevel, ProcessTokenElevation, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel
| order by Timestamp desc
let PotatoNames = dynamic(["juicypotato", "rottenpotato", "sweetpotato", "godpotato", "roguepotato", "localpotato", "remotepotato", "printspoofer", "efspotato"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\w3wp.exe"
| extend ChildName = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where TokenElevationType in ("%%1936", "%%1937")  // Full or Default-elevated
   or CommandLine has_any (PotatoNames)
   or ChildName has_any (PotatoNames)
   or (SubjectUserSid == "S-1-5-18" and ParentProcessName endswith "\\w3wp.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, SubjectUserSid, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Potato Suite Privilege Escalation from IIS w3wp.exe
id: 9e3c12b8-1d6a-44e9-bf7c-2c0a3b8e15dc
description: Detects Potato-family (Juicy/Rotten/Sweet/God/Rogue/Local/Remote/PrintSpoofer/EFS) privilege escalation invoked from the IIS worker w3wp.exe, matching OP-512's observed SYSTEM escalation.
references:
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-threat-cluster-op-512-targets.html
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1134/001/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
    - attack.t1134.001
    - attack.t1068
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
status: experimental
detection:
    parent_iis:
        ParentImage|endswith: '\w3wp.exe'
    potato_keywords:
        - CommandLine|contains:
            - 'juicypotato'
            - 'rottenpotato'
            - 'sweetpotato'
            - 'godpotato'
            - 'roguepotato'
            - 'localpotato'
            - 'remotepotato'
            - 'printspoofer'
            - 'efspotato'
        - Image|contains:
            - 'potato'
            - 'printspoofer'
    condition: parent_iis and potato_keywords
falsepositives:
    - Authorized red team engagements
level: critical
source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) (@EventID:4688 OR @EventID:1) @ParentImage:(*\w3wp.exe OR *\W3WP.EXE) (@CommandLine:(*juicypotato* OR *JuicyPotato* OR *rottenpotato* OR *RottenPotato* OR *sweetpotato* OR *SweetPotato* OR *godpotato* OR *GodPotato* OR *roguepotato* OR *RoguePotato* OR *printspoofer* OR *PrintSpoofer* OR *efspotato* OR *EfsPotato*) OR @Image:(*potato* OR *Potato* OR *POTATO* OR *printspoofer* OR *PrintSpoofer*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^w3wp\.exe$/i
| (regex("(?i)(juicypotato|rottenpotato|sweetpotato|godpotato|roguepotato|localpotato|remotepotato|printspoofer|efspotato)", field=CommandLine)
   OR regex("(?i)(potato|printspoofer)", field=ImageFileName)
   OR IntegrityLevel="System")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, IntegrityLevel], function=[count(), min(@timestamp)])
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.process_integrity_level) as integrity from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="w3wp.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_path="*\\inetsrv\\w3wp.exe") (Processes.process_integrity_level="System" OR Processes.process_integrity_level="high") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="SYSTEM" OR process_name!="w3wp.exe" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.process_integrity_level) as integrity from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="w3wp.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_path="*\\inetsrv\\w3wp.exe") (Processes.process_integrity_level="System" OR Processes.process_integrity_level="high") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="SYSTEM" OR process_name!="w3wp.exe" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:

      article before alerting.
level: medium

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

let BadHashes = dynamic(["ee41e06ed96182ce80cd4544a6abd5d7719c4a5c0e5ddb266a83842d39b99b0a", "40d264cf9c73923932c3dfd52d20f46ff602be3fea8dc6ecc71aca46e6067bf5", "f70abe93212637d3ec2f6c5e058ccac0307ebf63e496f38588cbfc17a8f8a264", "eb141a43958802727a6c813452450c10b92704bea4474ee5fd87c0a1be326e2e", "e952c18272efa1c3d73d0a5381bcf443c02743fe", "f4d77958a12a0778283d3e679b24b18f82e332c4", "681075027553546c119ec447eb8df84633dcffce", "f8d93c1769e877aae7e7d5c289a467b5ae371c7a", "98ee964edeb5a988c3bba8ea1e57fe0e", "58d4eccc982c9e9b1b98aa62c514e53a", "84ad78b2bab946c3677fdc28ebd8a774", "95dc2289427ed29b8b996d0e3d1b78cb"]);

        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Hackers Exploit Critical Everest Forms Pro WordPress Plugin Flaw to Take Over Sites

The Hacker News
2026-06-05 14 use cases 7 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Threat actors are actively exploiting a critical security flaw in Everest Forms Pro, a WordPress plugin with about 4,000 active installations, to execute arbitrary code, leading to a complete site compromise. The vulnerability in question is CVE-2026-3300 (CVSS score: 9.8), a remote code execution bug impacting all versions of the plugin up to, and including, 1.9.12. A patch for the flaw was

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains

[LLM] Everest Forms Pro RCE exploit attempt from named source IPs Delivery High
Hunts inbound HTTP requests to vulnerable WordPress sites from the four IPv4 sources Wordfence attributed to the CVE-2026-3300 exploitation campaign. Highest fidelity signal since the IPs were named in the original advisory and have driven 29,300+ blocked attempts since 2026-04-13. Rationale: Wordfence's named source IPs are the highest-confidence pivot in the article. Combining IP source + WordPress admin-ajax/everest_forms URI keeps the false-positive surface near zero. Cross-checked with Wordfence's advisory and abuse.ch ThreatFox for IP reputation. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wordfence.com/blog/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/

[LLM] Everest Forms Pro Calculation Addon PHP injection payload in form submission Exploitation Medium
Hunts POST bodies to WordPress endpoints containing PHP code-context characters that escape sanitize_text_field() and reach eval() in process_filter(). Targets the specific injection shape described by Wordfence — single quotes followed by PHP functions like system, exec, base64_decode, or backticks. Rationale: Wordfence quotes the bug as 'concatenating user-submitted form field values into a PHP code string without proper escaping before passing it to eval()' — the discriminating signal is PHP-function tokens (system, exec, base64_decode, shell_exec, assert) plus single-quote-break characters in a POST to admin-ajax/everest_forms. Cross-checked the wp-json everest path against the Everest Forms plugin source. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wordfence.com/blog/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004

[LLM] WordPress rogue 'diksimarina' admin account creation request Installation High
Hunts the specific payload Wordfence saw most commonly in CVE-2026-3300 exploitation: creation of a WordPress administrator account named 'diksimarina' with email 'diksimarina@gmail.com'. Hardcoded IOCs from the original advisory. Rationale: 'diksimarina' and 'diksimarina@gmail.com' are verbatim IOCs from Wordfence's report cited in the article — extremely high-fidelity strings unlikely to appear organically in benign traffic. Searching across multiple log surfaces (WAF, IIS, App Service, syslog) catches the payload regardless of where it lands. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wordfence.com/blog/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1136/001/
ATT&CKT1136.001 T1078.003

[LLM] WordPress PHP worker spawning shell or download utility post-RCE Installation Medium
Hunts the post-exploit behaviour where the PHP/Apache/Nginx worker process spawns sh, bash, wget, curl, python, perl, or nc — the natural follow-on after process_filter() eval() succeeds and the attacker drops a webshell or pulls a second-stage payload. Rationale: The article's kill-chain note explicitly cites 'PHP/Apache/Nginx worker processes spawning unusual children (sh, curl, wget)' as the execution-phase pivot. Pairing the parent web-tier binary with download/shell child binaries follows the BluRaven process-tree pattern and avoids the anti-bare-process-execution smell. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1505.003 T1105

status: experimental
description: Detects PHP/Apache/Nginx worker processes spawning unix shells, curl/wget, python/perl, or nc - high-confidence post-RCE indicator on WordPress hosts following CVE-2026-3300 or similar PHP eval() exploitation.
references:

      - '/php-fpm8.2'

  condition: selection_parent and selection_child
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd) (@ParentImage:(*\php-cgi.exe OR *\php.exe OR *\w3wp.exe OR *\httpd.exe OR *\nginx.exe) OR @process.parent.executable.path:(*/php-fpm* OR */httpd OR */apache2 OR */nginx)) (@Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\certutil.exe OR *\bitsadmin.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\wget.exe) OR @process.executable.path:(*/sh OR */bash OR */wget OR */curl OR */python* OR */perl OR */nc OR */ncat OR */socat))

| ImageFileName=/(\/sh|\/bash|\/dash|\/wget|\/curl|\/python3?|\/perl|\/nc|\/ncat|\/socat|\\cmd\.exe|\\powershell\.exe|\\certutil\.exe|\\bitsadmin\.exe)$/i

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)

    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession

// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine

| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-3300")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId

          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.

VECT 2.0 Ransomware Can Damage Files Its Own Decryptor Cannot Reliably Restore

Cyber Security News
2026-06-05 5 use cases 1 technique 3 kill-chain phases detected

A new ransomware strain called VECT 2.0 is raising serious concerns among security professionals, and for a troubling reason — even if a victim pays the ransom, the attacker&#8217;s own decryptor may not fully restore their files. This is not a typical failure tied to weak defenses or victim error. Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("a7eadcf81dd6fda0dd6affefaffcb33b1d8f64ddec6e5a1772d028ef2a7da0f2", "58e17dd61d4d55fa77c7f2dd28dd51875b0ce900c1e43b368b349e65f27d6fdd", "e1fc59c7ece6e9a7fb262fc8529e3c4905503a1ca44630f9724b2ccc518d0c06", "8ee4ec425bc0d8db050d13bbff98f483fff020050d49f40c5055ca2b9f6b1c4d", "9c745f95a09b37bc0486bf0f92aad4a3d5548a939c086b93d6235d34648e683f", "e512d22d2bd989f35ebaccb63615434870dc0642b0f60e6d4bda0bb89adee27a") or SHA1 in~ ("a7eadcf81dd6fda0dd6affefaffcb33b1d8f64ddec6e5a1772d028ef2a7da0f2", "58e17dd61d4d55fa77c7f2dd28dd51875b0ce900c1e43b368b349e65f27d6fdd", "e1fc59c7ece6e9a7fb262fc8529e3c4905503a1ca44630f9724b2ccc518d0c06", "8ee4ec425bc0d8db050d13bbff98f483fff020050d49f40c5055ca2b9f6b1c4d", "9c745f95a09b37bc0486bf0f92aad4a3d5548a939c086b93d6235d34648e683f", "e512d22d2bd989f35ebaccb63615434870dc0642b0f60e6d4bda0bb89adee27a") or MD5 in~ ("a7eadcf81dd6fda0dd6affefaffcb33b1d8f64ddec6e5a1772d028ef2a7da0f2", "58e17dd61d4d55fa77c7f2dd28dd51875b0ce900c1e43b368b349e65f27d6fdd", "e1fc59c7ece6e9a7fb262fc8529e3c4905503a1ca44630f9724b2ccc518d0c06", "8ee4ec425bc0d8db050d13bbff98f483fff020050d49f40c5055ca2b9f6b1c4d", "9c745f95a09b37bc0486bf0f92aad4a3d5548a939c086b93d6235d34648e683f", "e512d22d2bd989f35ebaccb63615434870dc0642b0f60e6d4bda0bb89adee27a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("a7eadcf81dd6fda0dd6affefaffcb33b1d8f64ddec6e5a1772d028ef2a7da0f2", "58e17dd61d4d55fa77c7f2dd28dd51875b0ce900c1e43b368b349e65f27d6fdd", "e1fc59c7ece6e9a7fb262fc8529e3c4905503a1ca44630f9724b2ccc518d0c06", "8ee4ec425bc0d8db050d13bbff98f483fff020050d49f40c5055ca2b9f6b1c4d", "9c745f95a09b37bc0486bf0f92aad4a3d5548a939c086b93d6235d34648e683f", "e512d22d2bd989f35ebaccb63615434870dc0642b0f60e6d4bda0bb89adee27a") or SHA1 in~ ("a7eadcf81dd6fda0dd6affefaffcb33b1d8f64ddec6e5a1772d028ef2a7da0f2", "58e17dd61d4d55fa77c7f2dd28dd51875b0ce900c1e43b368b349e65f27d6fdd", "e1fc59c7ece6e9a7fb262fc8529e3c4905503a1ca44630f9724b2ccc518d0c06", "8ee4ec425bc0d8db050d13bbff98f483fff020050d49f40c5055ca2b9f6b1c4d", "9c745f95a09b37bc0486bf0f92aad4a3d5548a939c086b93d6235d34648e683f", "e512d22d2bd989f35ebaccb63615434870dc0642b0f60e6d4bda0bb89adee27a") or MD5 in~ ("a7eadcf81dd6fda0dd6affefaffcb33b1d8f64ddec6e5a1772d028ef2a7da0f2", "58e17dd61d4d55fa77c7f2dd28dd51875b0ce900c1e43b368b349e65f27d6fdd", "e1fc59c7ece6e9a7fb262fc8529e3c4905503a1ca44630f9724b2ccc518d0c06", "8ee4ec425bc0d8db050d13bbff98f483fff020050d49f40c5055ca2b9f6b1c4d", "9c745f95a09b37bc0486bf0f92aad4a3d5548a939c086b93d6235d34648e683f", "e512d22d2bd989f35ebaccb63615434870dc0642b0f60e6d4bda0bb89adee27a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["a7eadcf81dd6fda0dd6affefaffcb33b1d8f64ddec6e5a1772d028ef2a7da0f2", "58e17dd61d4d55fa77c7f2dd28dd51875b0ce900c1e43b368b349e65f27d6fdd", "e1fc59c7ece6e9a7fb262fc8529e3c4905503a1ca44630f9724b2ccc518d0c06", "8ee4ec425bc0d8db050d13bbff98f483fff020050d49f40c5055ca2b9f6b1c4d", "9c745f95a09b37bc0486bf0f92aad4a3d5548a939c086b93d6235d34648e683f", "e512d22d2bd989f35ebaccb63615434870dc0642b0f60e6d4bda0bb89adee27a"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] GHOST STADIUM FIFA lookalike domain resolution (fifa.bio/.center/.gold/.red/.sale/.shopping/.show/.ski) · [LLM] GHOST STADIUM PingIdentity SSO clone: external referrer hot-linking fifa.com static assets · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Massiv / Perseus (Cerberus-derived) Android banking trojan APK hash on managed endpoint · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] GHOST STADIUM phishing kit / Android trojan C2 IP egress (8 specific hosts) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] GHOST STADIUM FIFA lookalike domain resolution (fifa.bio/.center/.gold/.red/.sale/.shopping/.show/.ski) Delivery High
Detects DNS resolution or HTTP connection from corporate or employee endpoints to the specific FIFA World Cup 2026 lookalike domains attributed to GHOST STADIUM. Hits indicate a user followed a Facebook ad, Telegram/WhatsApp link or SEO result into the cloned PingIdentity SSO phishing kit. Rationale: Domain list is the exact GHOST STADIUM cluster registered since August 2025 (per Group-IB tracking cited in the article). These are not legitimate FIFA properties — fifa.com is the only legitimate root — so any internal endpoint resolving them is high-fidelity initial-access signal. Cross-checked against the kill-chain Phase 1 IOCs. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/fifa-world-cup-2026-scams-are-already.html

[LLM] GHOST STADIUM phishing kit / Android trojan C2 IP egress (8 specific hosts) Command & Control High
Detects outbound connections from any internal endpoint (workstation, mobile via NAT, server) to the eight IP addresses that host the cloned fifa.com phishing infrastructure and serve as C2 for the Massiv/Perseus Android banking trojans. Article-specific IP set, not a reputation feed. Rationale: These are the exact infrastructure IPs Group-IB enumerated for the GHOST STADIUM cluster cited in the article. Eight discrete /32 destinations — small enough to enumerate, large enough to span the cloned-site fleet and the trojan C2. Any internal-to-IP connection is high-signal because none of these IPs front legitimate enterprise services. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/fifa-world-cup-2026-scams-are-already.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1437.001 T1583.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteIP in (GhostStadiumC2)
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionAttempt","InboundConnectionAccepted")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc

| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Massiv / Perseus (Cerberus-derived) Android banking trojan APK hash on managed endpoint Installation High
Detects the three specific SHA1 hashes of the trojanised RojaDirecta-style streaming APKs distributed alongside the World Cup 2026 fraud campaign. Matches against any file-write or download channel (browser saves, MDM-relayed install records, USB transfers) where the bytes touch a corporate-managed device. Rationale: These three SHA1 hashes are explicitly named in the kill-chain Phase 2 IOCs as the Massiv/Perseus APKs. SHA1 collisions across legitimate software are vanishingly rare; the APK extension + streaming-themed filename adds defense in depth for catching repacks even if the exact hash drifts. Highest-confidence host-side signal in the campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/fifa-world-cup-2026-scams-are-already.html
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1660 T1626.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem

DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA1 in (MassivPerseusHashes) or (FileName endswith ".apk" and (FileName has_any ("roja","directa","fifa","worldcup","stream","futbol","soccer")))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, SHA256, FileOriginUrl, FileOriginReferrerUrl, FileOriginIP
| order by Timestamp desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileSHA1 in (MassivPerseusHashes)
   or (TargetFileExtension =~ "apk" and TargetFileName has_any ("roja","directa","fifa","worldcup","stream","futbol","soccer"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA1, TargetFileSHA256

[LLM] GHOST STADIUM PingIdentity SSO clone: external referrer hot-linking fifa.com static assets Delivery Medium
Detects the signature visual-evasion technique of the GHOST STADIUM phishing kit — the cloned login page hot-links images directly from fifa.com so that brand-similarity scanners see the assets as legitimate. Hunts for outbound requests to fifa.com static-asset paths whose Referer header is NOT a fifa.com hostname. Rationale: The article explicitly describes this evasion: "It loads its images straight from FIFA's own servers, so the page looks authentic and slips past tools that flag copied images." Hot-linking inverts the normal Referer relationship — a phishing page loads fifa.com/<asset> with its own non-fifa hostname in the Referer header. Whitelisting fifa.com itself, PingIdentity (the real SSO provider), and search engines isolates the phishing-kit traffic shape. This is the rare detection that catches the kit's structural choice, not just the rotating IOC list. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/fifa-world-cup-2026-scams-are-already.html
ATT&CKT1656 T1036.005 T1608.005
Data sourcesWeb.Web
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","HttpConnectionInspected")
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend RemoteUrlLower = tolower(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrlLower has "fifa.com"
| where RemoteUrlLower matches regex @"fifa\.com/.+\.(jpg|jpeg|png|svg|webp|gif|css)(\?|$)"
   or RemoteUrlLower has_any ("fifa.com/assets/","fifa.com/static/","fifa.com/images/","fifa.com/_next/")
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType == "BrowserLaunchedToOpenUrl" or AdditionalFields has "Referrer"
    | extend Referrer = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).Referrer)
    | where isnotempty(Referrer) and Referrer !contains "fifa.com" and Referrer !contains "pingidentity.com"
    | project DeviceId, RefTime=Timestamp, Referrer
  ) on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (RefTime .. RefTime + 30s)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, Referrer, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP
| order by Timestamp desc
let LegitimateReferrers = dynamic(["fifa.com","www.fifa.com","pingidentity.com","ping.fifa.com","fifa.tm","ticketing.fifa.com"]);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Url matches regex @"(?i)fifa\.com/.+\.(jpg|jpeg|png|svg|webp|gif|css)(\?|$)"
   or Url has_any ("fifa.com/assets/","fifa.com/static/","fifa.com/images/","fifa.com/_next/")
| extend ReferrerHost = tolower(tostring(parse_url(HttpRequestHeaderReferer).Host))
| where isnotempty(HttpRequestHeaderReferer)
| where not (ReferrerHost in (LegitimateReferrers))
| where not (ReferrerHost endswith ".fifa.com")
| where ReferrerHost !has "google." and ReferrerHost !has "bing." and ReferrerHost !has "duckduckgo."
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, ReferrerHost, Url, HttpRequestHeaderReferer, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
@http.url:(*fifa.com/assets/* OR *fifa.com/static/* OR *fifa.com/images/* OR *fifa.com/_next/* OR *fifa.com/*.jpg OR *fifa.com/*.png OR *fifa.com/*.svg) -@http.referrer:(*fifa.com* OR *pingidentity.com* OR *google.* OR *bing.*) -@http.referer:(*fifa.com* OR *pingidentity.com* OR *google.* OR *bing.*)

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
