Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High
Classic macro/exploit pattern — Office app launching cmd/powershell/wmic/regsvr32.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.005 T1218
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\winword.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\excel.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\powerpnt.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\outlook.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\onenote.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\mspub.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\visio.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a") or SHA1 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a") or MD5 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a") or SHA1 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a") or MD5 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Cisco SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20245 exploitation via vconfd tenant-list upload
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Article-specific behavioural hunt — Cisco warns of unpatched SD-WAN zero-day exploited in attacks
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Cisco SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20245 exploitation via vconfd tenant-list upload Exploitation High
Hunts the literal Mandiant/Cisco PSIRT IOC published for CVE-2026-20245: the vScript daemon on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager (formerly vManage) logging a 'Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number' event in /var/log/scripts.log that invokes /usr/bin/vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh with an attacker-controlled -cli path argument. A successful exploit yields root via command injection in the tenant-list parser; the attacker must already hold netadmin (chained from CVE-2026-20182 or CVE-2026-20127), so any hit warrants immediate investigation of preceding admin-tier auth. Rationale: Anchors on three verbatim strings from the Cisco PSIRT example log line: the vScript syslog tag, the literal phrase 'Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number', and the path /usr/bin/vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh. All three appearing together on the same record is the exact IOC Cisco told customers to grep for in /var/log/scripts.log. The extracted -cli path argument is exposed for triage so analysts can immediately judge whether the uploaded file sits in a sane tenant-config directory or in /home, /tmp etc. (the malicious.csv example sits in /home/admin). Defender/Falcon/CloudWatch are empty because vManage is a Cisco appliance, not an EDR-managed endpoint or AWS resource. No external corroboration sought — the article reproduces the vendor advisory IOC verbatim and the CVE is too fresh (June 2026) for second-source IOC bundles to exist yet.
ATT&CKT1190 T1068 T1059.004
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SyslogMessage has "vScript"
    and SyslogMessage has "Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number"
    and SyslogMessage has "vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh"
| extend UploadPath = extract(@"-cli\s+path\s+(\S+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend VpnId = extract(@"vpn\s+(\d+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend SuspiciousPath = iff(UploadPath matches regex @"^/(home|tmp|var/tmp|dev/shm)/", "yes", "no")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, Facility, ProcessName, UploadPath, VpnId, SuspiciousPath, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

PCPJack Hijacks 230 AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure Servers for Covert SMTP Relay Network

The Hacker News
2026-06-05 14 use cases 5 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The threat actor known as PCPJack has hijacked cloud servers associated with Amazon Web Services (AWS), Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure to create a covert SMTP email relay network. "Compromised business servers across the U.S., Europe, and Asia were quietly converted into SMTP proxies, verified for mail relay capability, and synced to a downstream consumer every five minutes," Hunt.io said in

[LLM] Outbound C2 to PCPJack Sliver server 213.136.80.73 (esp. port 9000) Command & Control High
Detect any host beaconing to the PCPJack Sliver C2 IP 213.136.80.73 — particularly the port 9000 health-check the diagnostic script polls and the SCP/SSH (22) and HTTPS callbacks beacons use. Highest-confidence indicator in the article: the C2 IP itself was confirmed open and live by Hunt.io. Rationale: 213.136.80.73 is the unauthenticated PCPJack C2 server Hunt.io confirmed live with ports 8444/9443/9000 exposed; pivoting on the IP alone is high-fidelity. Cross-checked Hunt.io's write-up and the prior SentinelOne PCPJack analysis. Cross-checked against: • https://hunt.io/blog/pcpjack-230-cloud-servers-smtp-proxy-network-sliver-chisel • https://www.sentinelone.com/labs/cloud-worm-evicts-teampcp-and-steals-credentials-at-scale/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1571
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "213.136.80.73"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol, ActionType, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| extend Port9000Health = iif(RemotePort == 9000, "yes", "no")
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DestinationIP == "213.136.80.73"
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcHost=SourceHostName, SrcIP=SourceIP, DstIP=DestinationIP, DstPort=DestinationPort, AppProto=ApplicationProtocol, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, DeviceAction),
(ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DstIpAddr == "213.136.80.73"
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcHost=SrcHostname, SrcIP=SrcIpAddr, DstIP=DstIpAddr, DstPort=DstPortNumber, AppProto=NetworkApplicationProtocol, NetProto=NetworkProtocol, EventVendor, EventProduct, DvcAction)
| extend Port9000Health = iif(DstPort == 9000, "yes", "no")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] PCPJack SMTP quality-gate probe to smtp.gmail.com:587 from non-mail Linux workloads Actions on Objectives High
Hunt for the Sliver deployer's outbound 'mail relay capability' probe to smtp.gmail.com:587, which the script uses to filter beacons worth keeping. A cloud VM (AWS/GCP/Azure) opening port 587 to gmail from a non-mail workload is a sharp PCPJack-specific signal. Rationale: The article's SMTP quality gate is literally a TCP 587 probe to smtp.gmail.com — extremely specific behaviour for a non-mail workload. Confirmed by Hunt.io's primary source. Cross-checked against: • https://hunt.io/blog/pcpjack-230-cloud-servers-smtp-proxy-network-sliver-chisel
ATT&CKT1090 T1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemotePort == 587
| where RemoteUrl =~ "smtp.gmail.com" or RemoteUrl endswith ".gmail.com"
| where DeviceName !in~ (dynamic(["mailrelay01","mailrelay02"]))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where DestinationPort == 587
  | where DestinationHostName has "smtp.gmail.com" or DestinationDnsDomain has "gmail.com"
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcHost=SourceHostName, SrcIP=SourceIP, DstHost=DestinationHostName, DstIP=DestinationIP, DstPort=DestinationPort, AppProto=ApplicationProtocol),
(ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where DstPortNumber == 587
  | where DstHostname has "smtp.gmail.com" or DstDomain has "gmail.com"
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcHost=SrcHostname, SrcIP=SrcIpAddr, DstHost=DstHostname, DstIP=DstIpAddr, DstPort=DstPortNumber, AppProto=NetworkApplicationProtocol, NetProto=NetworkProtocol)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] SCP exfiltration of PCPJack proxy lists to downstream collector 38.242.204.245 Actions on Objectives High

Hunt for SSH/SCP/rsync connections to this IP, or process events showing scp/sftp invoking this destination on Linux beacons. Rationale: 38.242.204.245 is the named downstream collector receiving five-minute SCP syncs; pairing the IP with scp/rsync command-line keeps FP low. Confirmed by Hunt.io. [LLM] PCPJack hidden Chisel implant drop at /var/tmp/.xs on Linux Installation High
On the victim side the Sliver/Chisel binary is dropped as the hidden dot-prefixed file /var/tmp/.xs. Detect creation of this exact path, or any executable written to /var/tmp/ whose name starts with '.', then chmod'd +x. Rationale: /var/tmp/.xs is an exact path called out in the article as the persistence location for the Sliver/Chisel binary. Filtering well-known dot dirs keeps FPs minimal. Cross-checked against: • https://hunt.io/blog/pcpjack-230-cloud-servers-smtp-proxy-network-sliver-chisel
ATT&CKT1564.001 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FolderPath startswith "/var/tmp/"
| where FileName startswith "." and FileName !in~ (".X11-unix",".ICE-unix",".font-unix")
| extend IsXs = iif(FolderPath == "/var/tmp/.xs" or FileName == ".xs", "yes", "no")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, IsXs
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileCreate")
| where TargetFilePath startswith "/var/tmp/"
| where TargetFileName startswith "." and TargetFileName !in~ (".X11-unix",".ICE-unix",".font-unix")
| extend IsXs = iif(TargetFilePath == "/var/tmp/.xs" or TargetFileName == ".xs", "yes", "no")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, IsXs
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] PCPJack SOCKS5 listener bound to deterministic port 10000-14999 on Linux Command & Control Medium
The deployer derives each beacon's SOCKS5 proxy port from an MD5 of its Sliver UUID, mapped to 10000-14999. Hunt for newly-bound listeners in that port range on Linux servers, especially when the listener is a non-standard binary in /var/tmp or /tmp. Rationale: The 10000-14999 SOCKS5 port range is explicitly called out and derived from MD5(UUID); restricting to listeners spawned from /var/tmp or /tmp narrows it to PCPJack-likely cases. Cross-checked against: • https://hunt.io/blog/pcpjack-230-cloud-servers-smtp-proxy-network-sliver-chisel
ATT&CKT1090.001 T1571
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("ListeningConnectionCreated","InboundConnectionAccepted")
| where LocalPort between (10000 .. 14999)
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "/var/tmp/" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "/tmp/" or InitiatingProcessFileName startswith "."
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, LocalIP, LocalPort, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where NetworkDirection in ("Inbound","Listen")
| where SrcPortNumber between (10000 .. 14999) or DstPortNumber between (10000 .. 14999)
| extend Port = coalesce(SrcPortNumber, DstPortNumber)
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), DistinctPorts=dcount(Port), PortList=make_set(Port,50), Connections=count() by DvcHostname, EventVendor, EventProduct
| where DistinctPorts >= 1
| order by FirstSeen desc
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @SourcePort:[10000 TO 14999]) OR (source:linux.auditd @network.client.port:[10000 TO 14999] @process.executable.path:(\/var\/tmp\/* OR \/tmp\/.*))

[LLM] PCPJack exit-IP enrichment lookups to api.ipify.org and ip-api.com from Linux workloads Reconnaissance Medium
After SMTP-gate verification PCPJack enriches each proxy with exit IP, country, and ASN via api.ipify.org and ip-api.com. Linux servers calling these enrichment services back-to-back (especially right after suspicious SMTP probing) are likely PCPJack-converted relays. Rationale: api.ipify.org and ip-api.com are named in the article as the enrichment path PCPJack uses to label proxies. Two distinct lookups from the same host is a strong PCPJack-shape signal. Cross-checked against: • https://hunt.io/blog/pcpjack-230-cloud-servers-smtp-proxy-network-sliver-chisel
ATT&CKT1016 T1590.005
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
let Enrichers = dynamic(["api.ipify.org","ip-api.com","ipinfo.io","ifconfig.me","icanhazip.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl in~ (Enrichers) or RemoteUrl has_any (Enrichers)
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), HostsHit=make_set(RemoteUrl,10), Hits=count() by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| where array_length(HostsHit) >= 2 or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "/var/tmp/" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "/tmp/"
| order by FirstSeen desc
let Enrichers = dynamic(["api.ipify.org","ip-api.com","ipinfo.io","ifconfig.me","icanhazip.com"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where DnsQuery in~ (Enrichers) or DnsQuery has_any (Enrichers)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=SrcHostname, SrcIP=SrcIpAddr, Query=DnsQuery, EventVendor, EventProduct),
(ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where HttpHostName in~ (Enrichers) or Url has_any (Enrichers)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=SrcHostname, SrcIP=SrcIpAddr, Query=HttpHostName, Url, HttpMethod)
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Lookups=make_set(Query,10), Hits=count() by Host, SrcIP
| where array_length(Lookups) >= 2
| order by FirstSeen desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] Stata binary spawning OS shell (CVE-2026-47708 stata-mcp log_file_name injection) Exploitation High
Detects the Stata executable (or its Linux/macOS variants) spawning cmd/powershell/sh/bash/python child processes. This is the direct exploitation signal for CVE-2026-47708, where an attacker injects Stata's `shell` command via the unsanitised log_file_name parameter on the MCP `stata_do` tool, breaking out of the `log using "..."` string to execute arbitrary OS commands. Rationale: The article states the injection breaks out of the Stata `log using "..."` string so that `shell <cmd>` is interpreted as a Stata command, which then spawns an OS shell. Stata processes (stata.exe, stata-mp.exe, stata-se.exe, stata-be.exe, xstata variants) legitimately almost never spawn cmd/powershell/sh/bash/python children, so the parent-child pivot from the article's exploitation primitive is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory body (GHSA-4p62-hqp5-g644) and the linked fix commit which confirms log_file_name was interpolated raw into the Stata command string. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4p62-hqp5-g644 • https://github.com/SepineTam/stata-mcp/commit/e6f945941ae0c7cf5e74a428e0b3dc82b396382f • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
ATT&CKT1059 T1190 T1059.003 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("stata.exe","stata-mp.exe","stata-se.exe","stata-be.exe","xstata.exe","xstata-mp.exe","xstata-se.exe","stata","stata-mp","stata-se","stata-be")
| where FileName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","zsh.exe","bash","sh","zsh","python.exe","python","python3")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("stata.exe","stata-mp.exe","stata-se.exe","stata-be.exe","xstata.exe","xstata-mp.exe","xstata-se.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","python.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, AccountName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ProcessId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

      - '\stata-se.exe'
      - '\stata-be.exe'
      - '\xstata.exe'

  selection_child:

#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(stata|stata-mp|stata-se|stata-be|xstata|xstata-mp|xstata-se)(\.exe)?$/i

[LLM] Stata-authored log file written with shell metacharacters or path traversal in filename (CVE-2026-47708) Exploitation High
Detects file writes by Stata or the stata-mcp Python wrapper where the target `.log` filename contains shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&`, backtick, single/double quotes) or path traversal (`..`). The article shows the PoC produces a literal log file whose filename contains the injected payload — even if the `shell` portion fails, the file artifact itself is a deterministic exploitation footprint. Rationale: The article's PoC explicitly shows the generated path becomes `<log_dir>/'; shell echo pwned > /tmp/pwned.txt; '.log` — i.e. the log filename literally contains a semicolon, single-quote, and redirection metacharacters, and (per `generate_log_file` having no path-traversal guard) may also contain `..`. Both observations come directly from the article's source-code excerpts and PoC. Filtering DeviceFileEvents to Stata/Python writers with `.log` extension narrows scope to near-zero baseline, and the regex on metacharacters/traversal isolates the exploitation artefact from any legitimate workflow. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4p62-hqp5-g644 • https://github.com/SepineTam/stata-mcp/commit/e6f945941ae0c7cf5e74a428e0b3dc82b396382f
ATT&CKT1190 T1059 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("stata.exe","stata-mp.exe","stata-se.exe","stata-be.exe","xstata.exe","xstata-mp.exe","xstata-se.exe","python.exe","python","python3")
| where FileName endswith ".log"
| where FileName matches regex @"[;|&`'\"]|\.\."
     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("stata_mcp","stata-mcp","log_file_name")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated" or EventType == "FileModified"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("stata.exe","stata-mp.exe","stata-se.exe","stata-be.exe","xstata.exe","xstata-mp.exe","xstata-se.exe","python.exe","python","python3")
| where TargetFileName endswith ".log"
| where TargetFileName matches regex @"[;|&`'\"]|\.\."
     or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("stata_mcp","stata-mcp","log_file_name")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Detects .log files written by Stata or the stata-mcp Python wrapper whose filename contains shell metacharacters (semicolon, pipe, backtick, quote) or path traversal sequences, the deterministic artefact of CVE-2026-47708 exploitation against unpatched stata-mcp installations (<1.17.3).
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4p62-hqp5-g644
  - https://github.com/SepineTam/stata-mcp/commit/e6f945941ae0c7cf5e74a428e0b3dc82b396382f

detection:

      - '\stata-be.exe'
      - '\xstata.exe'
      - '\xstata-mp.exe'
      - '\xstata-se.exe'
      - '\python.exe'
  selection_ext:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.log'

      - '`'
      - "'"
      - '"'
      - '..'

falsepositives:

level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\\stata.exe OR *\\STATA.exe OR *\\stata-mp.exe OR *\\stata-se.exe OR *\\stata-be.exe OR *\\xstata.exe OR *\\python.exe) @TargetFilename:(*.log) @TargetFilename:(*\;* OR *\|* OR *\&* OR *..* OR *\`* OR *\'* OR *\"*)

| ContextImageFileName=/(stata|stata-mp|stata-se|stata-be|xstata|xstata-mp|xstata-se|python3?)(\.exe)?$/i
| TargetFileName=/\.log$/i
| regex("[;|&`'\"]|\\.\\.", field=TargetFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())

[LLM] Magecart skimmer payload fetched from Stripe customer record cus_TfFjAAZQNOYENR Delivery High
Hunts browser/proxy egress to api.stripe.com URLs that reference the specific Stripe customer record Sansec identified as the dead-drop hosting the obfuscated skimmer JavaScript. Catches the GTM-loaded skimmer's payload-fetch step on any corporate endpoint that visits a compromised Magento/Adobe Commerce checkout page. Rationale: The Stripe customer ID `cus_TfFjAAZQNOYENR` is the single highest-fidelity IOC in the article — Sansec named it as the specific dead-drop record holding the obfuscated skimmer JS that the malicious GTM container fetches. Stripe customer IDs are random 14-char tokens unique per account, so a literal match has effectively zero collision risk. Falcon left empty because FDR's DnsRequest/NetworkConnectIP4 events do not carry URL paths and the IOC lives inside the HTTPS URL — only TLS-inspecting proxy ingest would surface it. CloudWatch left empty (not AWS telemetry). Cross-checked against Sansec research index and Source Defense's coverage of the related Firestore/Braintree variant. Cross-checked against: • https://sansec.io/ • https://sansec.io/tags/skimmer • https://sourcedefense.com/resources/sd-research/new-magecart-attack-abuses-google-firestore-and-paypals-braintree-api/
ATT&CKT1102.001 T1059.007 T1189

  | where RemoteUrl has "cus_TfFjAAZQNOYENR"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
            InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
),
( DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where RemoteUrl has "cus_TfFjAAZQNOYENR" or AdditionalFields has "cus_TfFjAAZQNOYENR"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteUrl, AdditionalFields,
            InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
)
| order by Timestamp desc

  | where RequestURL has "cus_TfFjAAZQNOYENR"
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, RequestURL, DestinationHostName, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct
),
( ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Url has "cus_TfFjAAZQNOYENR"

),
( W3CIISLog

  | where csUriQuery has "cus_TfFjAAZQNOYENR" or csUriStem has "cus_TfFjAAZQNOYENR"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csUserName, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserAgent
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Magecart skimmer payload fetched from Firestore project braintree-payment-app Delivery High
Hunts browser/proxy egress to firestore.googleapis.com URLs that reference the Sansec-named Firestore project `braintree-payment-app` and/or the document path `tracking/captcha`. This is the Firestore variant of the same skimmer family — the malicious GTM container pulls the payload from this disguised-as-CAPTCHA document and stages stolen card data under localStorage key `_d_data_customer_` before exfiltrating via PayPal Braintree's sandbox GraphQL. Rationale: `braintree-payment-app` is a Firestore project name Sansec specifically called out, deliberately chosen to look like PayPal Braintree bot-protection traffic — almost no legitimate site would reach a project of that exact name. `tracking/captcha` is the document path. Pair of strings tightly bounds FPs to ~zero outside of the campaign. Cross-corroborated with Source Defense's independent write-up confirming the same project/document and that exfil rides PayPal Braintree's sandbox GraphQL customer-create call. Falcon includes a hunting-tier DnsRequest pivot since Firebase project subdomains (braintree-payment-app.firebaseio.com / .web.app / .firebaseapp.com) sometimes resolve and would show in DNS even without URL inspection. Cross-checked against: • https://sourcedefense.com/resources/sd-research/new-magecart-attack-abuses-google-firestore-and-paypals-braintree-api/ • https://sansec.io/ • https://sansec.io/tags/web-skimming
ATT&CKT1102.001 T1059.007 T1567 T1189
Data sourcesWeb
union isfuzzy=true
( DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where RemoteUrl has "braintree-payment-app"
     or RemoteUrl has "projects/braintree-payment-app"
     or (RemoteUrl has "firestore.googleapis.com" and RemoteUrl has "tracking/captcha")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl,
            InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
),
( DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where RemoteUrl has "braintree-payment-app" or AdditionalFields has "braintree-payment-app" or AdditionalFields has "_d_data_customer_"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteUrl, AdditionalFields,
            InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
)
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
( CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where (DestinationHostName has "firestore.googleapis.com" or RequestURL has "firestore.googleapis.com")
  | where RequestURL has "braintree-payment-app" or RequestURL has "tracking/captcha"
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, RequestURL, DestinationHostName, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor
),
( ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where HttpHostName has "firestore.googleapis.com"
  | where Url has "braintree-payment-app" or Url has "projects/braintree-payment-app" or Url has "tracking/captcha"
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, HttpHostName, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, EventVendor
),
( ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any ("braintree-payment-app.firebaseio.com", "braintree-payment-app.web.app", "braintree-payment-app.firebaseapp.com")
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DnsQuery, EventVendor
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm exfiltration to t.m-kosche.com OpenTelemetry endpoint Actions on Objectives High
Detects DNS/HTTP egress to the TeamPCP exfiltration C2 at t.m-kosche.com, where stolen creds are POSTed to /api/public/otel/v1/traces masquerading as OpenTelemetry traffic. High-fidelity because the FQDN and URI path are unique to this campaign and corroborated by Wiz, Snyk and Socket. Rationale: Pivots on the exact exfil FQDN (t.m-kosche.com) and the unique OpenTelemetry-disguise URI path (/api/public/otel/v1/traces) called out in Wiz, Snyk and Socket write-ups of the same Mini Shai-Hulud / TeamPCP wave that published @cap-js/openapi@1.4.1 on 2026-05-19. Both strings are unambiguous IOCs with no benign collisions. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-sap-npm • https://snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/ • https://socket.dev/blog/sap-cap-npm-packages-supply-chain-attack • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/monitoring-npm-supply-chain-attacks/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/mini-shai-hulud-pushes-malicious-antv.html

[LLM] Bun runtime spawned by npm/node preinstall hook (TeamPCP setup.mjs loader) Installation High
Detects the Mini Shai-Hulud execution chain where the compromised npm preinstall hook in @cap-js/openapi (and sibling packages) invokes the Bun JavaScript runtime to load setup.mjs → execution.js. Bun is rarely a child of npm/node in enterprise environments and is the campaign's signature loader. Rationale: Wiz and Socket both document the bun-runtime loader chain (preinstall→setup.mjs→bun→execution.js) as the Mini Shai-Hulud signature. Bun being spawned by npm/node is rare outside dedicated Bun shops, and pairing it with the `preinstall` / `setup.mjs` / `execution.js` strings caught in cmdline lifts confidence dramatically. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-sap-npm • https://socket.dev/blog/sap-cap-npm-packages-supply-chain-attack • https://snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/ • https://safedep.io/mini-shai-hulud-strikes-again-314-npm-packages-compromised/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1546.016
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// TeamPCP Mini Shai-Hulud: Bun spawned from npm preinstall
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "bun.exe" or FileName =~ "bun"
| where (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe","npm-cli.js","node","npm","yarn","pnpm","npx"))
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("preinstall","setup.mjs","execution.js")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("setup.mjs","execution.js")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
// TeamPCP Mini Shai-Hulud: Bun spawned from npm preinstall (Sentinel — SecurityEvent 4688 + ASIM)
union isfuzzy=true
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where NewProcessName endswith "\\bun.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "/bun"
  | where (ParentProcessName has_any ("\\npm.exe","\\node.exe","\\yarn.exe","\\pnpm.exe","\\npx.exe","/npm","/node","/yarn","/pnpm","/npx"))
       or CommandLine has_any ("setup.mjs","execution.js","preinstall")
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account=SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, Source="SecurityEvent"),
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where TargetProcessName endswith "bun.exe" or TargetProcessName endswith "/bun"
  | where (ParentProcessName has_any ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe"))
       or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("setup.mjs","execution.js")
       or ParentProcessCommandLine has "preinstall"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername, NewProcessName=TargetProcessName, CommandLine=TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, Source="ImProcessCreate")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud payload SHA256 on disk (7c24b4d9...e627144e8b) Installation High
Hash-based detection for the specific malicious payload binary tied to @cap-js/openapi@1.4.1 in GHSA-jpvj-wpmj-h7rv. Catches the file at write-time (DeviceFileEvents) and at any subsequent execution attempt — definitive identification with effectively zero FP risk. Rationale: Direct SHA256/SHA1 IOC pivots from the GHSA advisory itself. Hash-on-disk and hash-on-execution coverage closes both the install and the run pathway; multi-table union catches it whether the file lands during npm install, gets loaded as a DLL/module, or runs as a process. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jpvj-wpmj-h7rv • https://www.wiz.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-sap-npm

[LLM] Cloud/SSH/npm credential file access by Node or Bun during npm install Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for the credential harvesting stage of Mini Shai-Hulud: Node or Bun (when spawned within an npm install context) reading developer secret stores — ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh/id_*, gh hosts.yml, kubeconfig, .docker/config.json, Vault tokens. These files are read by the malware to enumerate cloud/CI credentials before exfil. Rationale: Wiz, Snyk, Socket and Unit42 all enumerate the same harvest target set (AWS/Azure/GCP/Kubernetes/GitHub/npm/SSH/Vault). Detecting node or bun in install-context fanning out across ≥3 of these distinct cred file types within a single process group is the highest-signal behavioural pivot the malware leaves before exfiltrating to t.m-kosche.com. Anti-pattern-aware: threshold and process gate suppress benign single-file reads (npm reads ~/.npmrc every install on its own). Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-sap-npm • https://snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/ • https://socket.dev/blog/sap-cap-npm-packages-supply-chain-attack • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/monitoring-npm-supply-chain-attacks/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
// Mini Shai-Hulud credential harvest: node/bun touching multiple secret stores during install
let credPaths = dynamic([
  @"\.aws\credentials", @"/.aws/credentials",
  @"\.aws\config", @"/.aws/config",
  @"\.npmrc", @"/.npmrc",
  @"\.ssh\id_", @"/.ssh/id_",
  @"\.ssh\known_hosts", @"/.ssh/known_hosts",
  @"\.config\gh\hosts.yml", @"/.config/gh/hosts.yml",
  @"\.kube\config", @"/.kube/config",
  @"\.docker\config.json", @"/.docker/config.json",
  @".vault-token",
  @"\AppData\Roaming\gcloud\credentials.db", @"/.config/gcloud/credentials.db",
  @"\.azure\msal_token_cache", @"/.azure/msal_token_cache"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileOpenInfo","FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","bun.exe","bun","npm.exe","npm","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("install","preinstall","setup.mjs","execution.js","npm ci","npm i ")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe")
| where FolderPath has_any (credPaths) or FileName has_any (credPaths)
| summarize HitCount = count(), PathsTouched = make_set(FolderPath, 50), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
  by DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| where HitCount >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
// Mini Shai-Hulud credential harvest via ASIM file events
let credPaths = dynamic([
  @"\.aws\credentials", @"/.aws/credentials",
  @"\.aws\config", @"/.aws/config",
  @"\.npmrc", @"/.npmrc",
  @"\.ssh\id_", @"/.ssh/id_",
  @"\.config\gh\hosts.yml", @"/.config/gh/hosts.yml",
  @"\.kube\config", @"/.kube/config",
  @"\.docker\config.json", @"/.docker/config.json",
  @".vault-token",
  @"/.config/gcloud/credentials.db",
  @"/.azure/msal_token_cache"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","bun","npm","yarn","pnpm")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("install","preinstall","setup.mjs","execution.js")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (credPaths) or TargetFileName has_any (credPaths)
| summarize HitCount = count(), PathsTouched = make_set(TargetFilePath, 50), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
  by Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| where HitCount >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
(source:windows.sysmon AND @EventID:11 AND @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\Node.exe OR *\NODE.EXE OR *\bun.exe OR *\Bun.exe OR *\BUN.EXE) AND @TargetFilename:(*\.aws\credentials* OR *\.aws\config* OR *\.npmrc* OR *\.ssh\id_* OR *\.config\gh\hosts.yml* OR *\.kube\config* OR *\.docker\config.json* OR *.vault-token* OR *\.azure\msal_token_cache*)) OR (source:linux.auditd AND @process.name:(node OR bun OR npm OR yarn OR pnpm) AND @file.path:(*/.aws/credentials* OR */.aws/config* OR */.npmrc* OR */.ssh/id_* OR */.config/gh/hosts.yml* OR */.kube/config* OR */.docker/config.json* OR */.vault-token* OR */.config/gcloud/credentials.db* OR */.azure/msal_token_cache*))
(#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo OR #event_simpleName=FileWritten) ContextImageFileName=/(node|bun|npm|yarn|pnpm)(\.exe)?$/i | TargetFileName=/(\\\.aws\\(credentials|config)|\/\.aws\/(credentials|config)|\\\.npmrc|\/\.npmrc|\\\.ssh\\id_|\/\.ssh\/id_|\\\.config\\gh\\hosts\.yml|\/\.config\/gh\/hosts\.yml|\\\.kube\\config|\/\.kube\/config|\\\.docker\\config\.json|\/\.docker\/config\.json|\.vault-token|\/\.config\/gcloud\/credentials\.db|\/\.azure\/msal_token_cache)/i | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId], function=[count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true, as=DistinctPaths), collect(TargetFileName)]) | DistinctPaths >= 3 | sort(DistinctPaths, order=desc)

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537") or SHA1 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537") or MD5 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537") or SHA1 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537") or MD5 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] AVideo YPTSocket plugin XSS injection via webSocketSelfURI/page_title query strings Exploitation High
Hunts unauthenticated exploitation of GHSA-8whc-2wmv-ww35 in WWBN AVideo by detecting HTTP requests to the YPTSocket token endpoint or WebSocket upgrade carrying HTML/JS payloads in the webSocketSelfURI or page_title query parameters. The payload is then broadcast to any admin viewing a page that renders the YPTSocket debug panel. Rationale: Anchored on the exact endpoint path /plugin/YPTSocket/ and the two attacker-controlled parameters (webSocketSelfURI, page_title) named in functions.php:21-24 and MessageSQLiteV2.php:91/110, combined with URL-encoded and raw HTML/JS payload tokens (including the article's String.fromCharCode evasion). Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory text and the AVideo repo paths cited in the PoC. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8whc-2wmv-ww35 • https://github.com/WWBN/AVideo

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
